Gemini CLI Community Digest — 2026-10-28

Today's Highlights

Three release channels advanced today: stable v0.66.0, v0.67.0-preview.0, and nightly v0.67.0-nightly.20261028, bringing Android/Termux ripgrep path fixes and CRLF-safe diffing. Issue traffic continues to concentrate on agent/subagent reliability — false GOAL success after MAX_TURNS, generalist-agent hangs, and 400 errors under large tool counts dominate the top of the queue. Community PRs this cycle are largely quality-of-life fixes: cancellation handling, \n escaping correctness, Unicode-safe truncation, and terminal resize performance.

Releases

v0.67.0-nightly.20261028.gfa5c17365

  • fix(core): allow trusted system paths on Android (Termux) for ripgrep resolution (#21836, @amelidev) — unblocks Termux users whose binary resolution was previously rejected.
  • fix(core): normalize CRLF line endings before diffing in getDiffContextSnippet (@jesussamuel-byte) — prevents spurious diff context on Windows/CRLF files.

v0.67.0-preview.0

  • Rolls up the v0.65.0 changelog, bumps the nightly baseline to 0.67.0-nightly.20261020.gb041de017, and includes the v0.66.0-preview changelog.

v0.66.0

  • ROADMAP.md updated to drop references to the outdated 2025 roadmap (#29723, @DavidAPierce).
  • Auto-generated changelog for v0.65.0-preview.0 plus routine version bumps.

Hot Issues

  1. #22323 — Subagent recovery after MAX_TURNS reported as GOAL success (P1, 13 comments, 👍2) The codebase_investigator subagent returns status: "success" / Termination Reason: "GOAL" even when it exhausted its turn budget before doing any analysis. This is the most-commented issue of the day because it silently corrupts agent-level observability — callers can't distinguish "done" from "gave up."

  2. #21409 — Generalist agent hangs (P1, 8 comments, 👍8) Highest-reaction issue in the queue. Any deferral to the generalist agent hangs indefinitely (even folder creation); users work around it by forbidding subagent use. Sustained 👍 growth signals broad reproduction.

  3. #19873 — Zero-dependency OS sandboxing & post-execution intent routing (P2, 9 comments) Architectural proposal to lean into Gemini 3's native bash affinity while keeping safety via sandbox + intent routing after execution. A key design thread for how much shell freedom the model gets.

  4. #21968 — Gemini does not use skills and sub-agents enough (P2, 7 comments) Anecdotal but widely echoed: custom skills/subagents only fire when explicitly instructed. Directly undermines the extensibility story the team is building.

  5. #24246 — 400 error with large tool counts (P2, 3 comments) Exceeding the tool budget produces a hard 400 instead of graceful scoping. (Title and body disagree on 128 vs. 400 tools — worth reconciling, since the threshold matters for MCP-heavy setups.)

  6. #22267 — Browser Agent ignores settings.json overrides (e.g. maxTurns) (P2, 4 comments) The AgentRegistry merges config correctly at init, but the Browser Agent bypasses it. A config-trust bug rather than a capability gap.

  7. #21983 — Browser subagent fails on Wayland (P1, 4 comments) Reports a GOAL termination despite failure — the same misleading-termination pattern as #22323, now on Linux/Wayland desktops.

  8. #22672 — Agent should stop/discourage destructive behavior (P2, 3 comments, 👍1) Model reaches for git reset / --force where safer alternatives exist, and lacks guardrails around stateful resources like databases.

  9. #22745 — Assess AST-aware file reads, search, and mapping (EPIC, 7 comments) Proposes AST-aware tools to cut misaligned reads, turn count, and token noise. Paired with #22746 and #22747 (tilth/glyph/ast-grep candidates).

  10. #22466 — Incorrect \n escape behavior (P2, 2 comments) Naive \n workaround logic corrupts string literals; now has a matching implementation PR (#29989), so this one is likely to close soon.

Key PR Progress

  1. #29977 — fix(core): honor cancellation in read_background_output (P2, help wanted) The tool ignored its abort signal: cancelled calls kept sleeping for the full delay_ms and then read the log anyway. Now rejects with AbortError up front.

  2. #29989 — fix(core,cli): incorrect \n escaping (P2, maintainer) Fixes multiple naive escape/unescape paths across core and CLI that corrupted valid \n sequences inside string literals, regexes, and code spans during edits.

  3. #29982 — fix(core): recognize dotted Gemini 3 models supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse() used startsWith('gemini-3-'), missing dotted model names when dynamic model configuration is disabled — silently degrading multimodal function responses.

  4. #29980 — feat(cli): gemini extensions validate <path> Adds pre-install/pre-publish validation of gemini-extension.json, including context file path security checks, plus evaluation tests.

  5. #29987 — fix(core): normalize leading slashes in @ autocomplete Makes @/, @/src, and @./package.json resolve correctly instead of returning no completions.

  6. #29993 — fix(ui): surrogate pairs in sanitizeForDisplay Truncation by UTF-16 code units could split an emoji's surrogate pair and drop the character; now truncates on code-point boundaries.

  7. #29965 — fix(cli): ExpandableText truncation and toggle behavior Companion Unicode fix plus toggle-state correctness in collapsed labels.

  8. #29904 — fix(cli): bound inline history re-render on terminal width change Directly targets #21924's flicker/perf complaints by bounding resize work in the inline renderer.

  9. #29988 — fix(vscode-ide-companion): track all Disposables (see also #29994) A stray pair of parentheses turned two registrations into a comma expression, leaking the gemini.diff.accept and workspace-folder listeners. Two independent community PRs converge on the same fix.

  10. #29995 — docs(readme): clarify scope, limitations, and tool landscape Consolidates three separate [!NOTE] banners into one scannable disclaimer plus a tool-selection guide — useful positioning work as the Google CLI surface expands.

Feature Request Trends

  • Agent observability and control. Recurring asks for truthful termination reasons, subagent trajectories surfaced via /chat share (#22598), and subagent context included in /bug reports (#21763).
  • Context frugality. AST-aware reads/search/mapping (#22745, #22746, #22747) and "Tactful Extraction" surgical read hierarchies (#19561) aim to shrink the ~36.6k-token per-turn baseline.
  • Persistent, out-of-context task state. Replace WriteToDo with file-based CRUD (#18836) and experiment with native file tools for the tracker (#21000).
  • Safety and sandboxing. Sandboxed bash with intent routing (#19873), discouraging destructive git/DB operations (#22672), and per-workspace rather than global policy (#18397).
  • Subagent ecosystem maturity. Settings-based subagent discovery (#18285), shared memory / parallel collaboration (#18287), and symlinked agent definitions (#20079).
  • Terminal UI polish. Flicker-free resize (#21924), ambiguous-width character handling, and Unicode-safe rendering.
  • Self-awareness. The CLI should accurately describe its own flags, hotkeys, and self-invocation (#21432).

Developer Pain Points

  • Hangs and misleading success states. The generalist agent hanging indefinitely (#21409) plus MAX_TURNS reported as GOAL success (#22323) and the Wayland browser agent reporting GOAL on failure (#21983) form a cluster: failures are both blocking and invisible.
  • Agent delegation is unreliable in both directions. Subagents either never trigger spontaneously (#21968) or hang when they do (#21409); Browser Agent settings overrides are ignored entirely (#22267).
  • Tool/config scaling limits. Large MCP/tool inventories trigger hard 400s (#24246), and models litter workspaces with ad-hoc temp scripts (#23571).
  • Cross-platform paper cuts. Termux/Android ripgrep resolution, Wayland browser sessions, Windows CRLF diffs, East Asian ambiguous-width terminals, and emoji truncation — a steady stream of environment-specific breakage this cycle.
  • Text-escaping correctness. Naive \n handling (#22466) is a high-frequency, low-tolerance class of bug because it silently mutates user code during edits.
  • Debuggability gap. /bug reports omit subagent internals (#21763), making the above failures hard to triage from user reports alone.

  • BYOK and multi-provider flexibility is the loudest theme: multi-model switching within one session (#3709), per-agent provider selection (#4703), credential commands in providers.json/managed settings (#4936), and preserving MCP tool images under BYOK (#4600).
  • ACP / headless parity with the interactive CLI: contextTier config (#4275), plugin skills in ACP sessions (#5269), working /rename (#5115), and silent OAuth resolution (#4994).
  • Enterprise deployment and policy controls: system-wide Windows installer (#5129), allowedMcpServers matching fixes (#4989), and org-level custom agent visibility (#3572).
  • MCP extensibility: server-provided prompts (#505) and reliable multimodal tool results (#4600).
  • Session lifecycle management: unarchive/restore sessions (#3518, 👍11), inline plan annotations (#4563), and durable event delivery (#5100).
  • Model routing transparency and tuning: configurable reasoning effort for Auto (#4560) and configurable retry/backoff counts (#3679).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Model selection is opaque and non-persistent. Settings revert between sessions (#1869), Auto forces reasoningEffort: null (#4560), and Auto picking GPT-6.1 Sol can hang the Plan → Implementation transition (#5270).
  • Retry/throttling behavior wastes time and quota. Aggressive 429 retries (#2760) and Azure BYOK exhausting five retries in ~0.15s (#3679) are recurring complaints.
  • Platform reliability gaps. Windows native crashes across multiple versions (#4026), WSL2 voice segfaults (#5197), and broken copy/paste over SSH + tmux (#3260).
  • Silent failures are worse than errors. preToolUse hooks bypassed under parallel tool calls (#2893), dropped MCP images (#4600), missing task_complete output (#2482), and /rename reporting false success (#5115).
  • Enterprise constraints block adoption. User-profile installs conflict with security policy (#5129), and allow-list matching plus org agent discovery remain unreliable (#4989, #3572).
  • Session durability is fragile. A single 120s host-ack timeout can render a session unusable until resume (#5100), and archived sessions cannot be restored (#3518).
OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-10-28

1. Today's Highlights

OpenCode v2.2.0 shipped with experimental Desktop plugins, opening the desktop client to community-built extensions for the first time. Issue activity remains dominated by the free-tier limit mega-thread (#59387, 35 comments) and a cluster of high-severity Windows/WSL regressions. On the PR side, core contributors landed a process-daemon readiness refactor stack and are trimming unused AI SDK provider bundles from packages/core.

2. Releases

v2.2.0

  • Desktop plugins (experimental) — create, install, and share desktop GUI plugins. Merged via #55246, #59469, #59489.
  • Docs: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/gui
  • Notable: API surface is explicitly experimental, so plugin authors should expect breaking changes before stabilization.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #59387 — Free tier issues: read this first (35 comments, 👍7)
    Canonical triage thread for Free usage exceeded, non-resetting daily limits, and Desktop version gating. High comment volume without resolution suggests the free-tier quota path still lacks clear diagnostics — the most active issue in the repo right now.

  2. #52237 — Remote MCP servers that fail once are never retried (13 comments)
    After a transient failure (notably macOS sleep/wake killing long-lived HTTP connections), the background service pins the MCP server in failed state until restart. Restarting the TUI doesn't help because state lives in the daemon. This is a real reliability blocker for anyone depending on remote MCP tooling.

  3. #52266 — Windows: console window flashes ~1/sec (8 comments, 👍3)
    Missing CREATE_NO_WINDOW on spawn causes a visible console flash for every git.exe invocation. A re-report of #22414 and #31629 — a long-lived regression that keeps resurfacing, which is why it's drawing 👍.

  4. #53011 — edit tool duplicates numeric replacement values (8 comments)
    Replacing 640 with 900 produced 900900, with duplication factors observed from 2x to 129x. Silent file corruption in the core edit path — [triaging] status but clearly the highest-risk correctness bug in the list.

  5. #52378 — Failed subagent reported to parent as success (8 comments)
    finish:"error" with MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL and empty content is surfaced as a successful child completion. Marked [reproduced]; this corrupts orchestration semantics for anyone building multi-agent workflows.

  6. #52363 — OpenAI models disappear when Zen or Go is connected (8 comments, severity:high)
    ChatGPT OAuth login succeeds and credentials store correctly, but the openai provider never registers — nothing selectable in /models. Affects all auth methods (browser and headless), so this is a full provider-registry break for OpenAI users.

  7. #52234 — Hardcoded port 49374 hangs silently when unavailable (7 comments)
    No fallback port, no bind error — the TUI sits on Starting background server... forever. Especially painful on WSL2/Hyper-V where the host unpredictably reserves ranges. Cheap fix, high user impact.

  8. #52154 — Message history is not isolated per session (7 comments, 👍2)
    Up-arrow recalls the last message from whichever session was most recent globally, not the current one. A papercut that compounds for users running many concurrent sessions — exactly the workflow OpenCode encourages.

  9. #52333 — provider.use deny policies bypassed during hot-reload (severity:high)
    There is a window during config/plugin reload where denied providers become selectable, and a prompt landing in that window silently routes system prompt + session history to a third-party free provider. A security issue, not just a correctness one.

  10. #52205 — Windows Desktop passes WSL UNC paths to Linux server (5 comments)
    Selecting a WSL folder returns \\wsl.localhost\..., which the Linux-side server can't handle — HTTP 500s and persistent startup crashes. [reproduced]; blocks the Windows-Desktop + WSL-server combo entirely.

Also worth watching: #52203 (Windows TUI survives terminal close, leaks CPU/memory), #52122 (Nix desktop arms the production auto-updater), #52178 (Zen API CORS only on /models, all inference preflights 404).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #59771 — Remove bundled Cohere, Vercel, Perplexity AI SDK packages
    Drops @ai-sdk/cohere, @ai-sdk/vercel, @ai-sdk/perplexity plus their now-redundant provider plugins and the unused createProviderPlugin helper. Meaningful bundle/lockfile slimming and a simplification of the provider plugin layer.

  2. #59700 / #59701 / #59702 — process-daemon control stack (jlongster)
    Routes stop/ownership through Control, replaces polling with readiness signals, and polls every 25 ms on Windows. Ported from opencode-pty; directly targets daemon lifecycle flakiness that underlies several of the issues above.

  3. #53233 — Honor compaction retained-text budget
    Fixes #43250 by enforcing the retained-text invariant, permitting an empty recent tail when no complete exchange fits. Long-lived fix (opened 2026-10-04) for context-compaction correctness.

  4. #59765 — Make provider model() settings optional, unify Config type
    Removes the mandatory {} argument and normalizes Config / LanguageModelOptions / Options naming across providers. Small DX win for anyone writing custom providers.

  5. #59773 — Stats: ignore requests rejected before routing
    Stops counting generation.completed events with attempts = 0, which were polluting the /data model dimension with phantom models. Cleans up public usage analytics.

  6. #59437 — feat(core): add /goal with a client-side done check
    Alternative to #58508: same idle hook, /goal command, and TUI, but no new session.settled server event and no native flag on the compaction hook. Clients derive "done" from already-synced data — a less invasive design for agentic loop control.

  7. #59403 — refactor(nix): fetch dependencies from bun.lock
    Closes #49063; eliminates hand-maintained platform-specific node_modules hashes. Removes a recurring Nix packaging maintenance burden.

  8. #59784 / #59783 / #59785 — session title filter, auth list account labels, copy full file from review
    Three community UX contributions from lancy69, each closing a request (#56843, #59040, #58878). All marked draft pending design approval — worth weighing in on the issues.

  9. #59630 — Upgrade Effect to 4.0.6
    Picks up the SQLite snowflake-ID rounding fix (Effect-TS/effect#9485). Low-risk dependency bump with a concrete data-integrity payoff.

  10. #59770 — TUI: navigate transcript with keypad Home/End
    Closes #55533 (re-filed after #57114 was closed). Fixes keypad-key handling under the kitty keyboard protocol.

5. Feature Request Trends

  • Configurability of endpoints and secrets — OPENCODE_PASSWORD_FILE (#52156) and editable base/console API URLs per provider (#52218). Users want container/secret-manager-friendly configuration and self-hosted/alternate gateways.
  • Multi-session ergonomics — per-session message history (#52154) and filtering session lists by title (PR #59784). A clear signal that heavy users now run many concurrent sessions.
  • CLI surface polish — distinguishing stored accounts in auth list (#59040) and aligning opencode mini's process controls with the main TUI: configurable exit and ctrl+z suspend (#52695).
  • Agentic loop control — /goal with a client-side done check (#59437), plus a browser API operation to close tabs (#59787, closed) so agents can clean up after themselves.
  • Review/UI affordances — copy full file contents from review (#58878) and gallery navigation in image preview (#58295).
  • Build provenance / observability — recording the pinned Electron version in the desktop debug export (#52125) so Nix builds can be distinguished from upstream binaries.

6. Developer Pain Points

  • Windows is the dominant source of friction. Console-window flashing (#52266), orphaned TUI processes after terminal close (#52203), EDITOR paths containing spaces breaking under Git-Bash (#52265), and WSL UNC paths crashing the Desktop↔server link (#52205). Several are re-reports (e.g. #22414, #31629), which reads as insufficient prioritization rather than novel breakage.
  • Provider/model registry inconsistency. Models vanish from the picker despite valid credentials (#52363, #52118) — auth succeeds but registration doesn't, with no surfaced error.
  • Silent failure instead of an error message. Hardcoded port 49374 hangs indefinitely (#52234); local plugins without a root entrypoint are skipped without warning (#52300); failed subagents are reported as successes (#52378). The recurring theme is missing diagnostics at failure boundaries.
  • Long-lived connection fragility. MCP servers never retried after one failure (#52237) — sleep/wake is the common trigger. Related to the process-daemon readiness work in PRs #59700–#59702.
  • Security policy gaps under reload. Deny-lists bypassable during hot-reload (#52333) erodes trust in experimental.policies for anyone running untrusted plugins.
  • Template $-sequence handling. Formatter args and prompt templates corrupt paths containing $&, $', $`, $$ (#52314) — a String.replace footgun repeated across several call sites.
  • Free-tier confusion. A 35-comment mega-thread (#59387) for quotas that appear not to reset suggests the messaging and/or the reset logic needs work before more users hit it.

Note: no Discussions data was provided for this period, so that section is omitted.

Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-10-28

1. Today's Highlights

No releases landed in the last 24 hours, but maintainers had a heavy triage day: a cluster of P0 and durable issues were closed around session resume losing built-in tools, OpenAI Responses tool replay, and Bedrock schema limits. On the open side, two long-running reliability concerns remain prominent — permanent session wedging at the context ceiling on reasoning models (#9409) and Anthropic streaming/tool-registration fragility (#10390, #11376).

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24h.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #10953 — OpenAI login fails with ChatGPT Business, legacy Codex login works [CLOSED] [no-action] · 11 comments · 👍3 The most-commented issue of the day: 3p_delegated_access_policy_denied blocks regular OpenAI subscription login for Business workspaces, while the legacy Codex path succeeds. Closed as no-action, but auth/policy mismatch for enterprise workspaces is likely to resurface. Link

  2. #9409 — Sessions wedge permanently at the context ceiling on reasoning models [OPEN] · 10 comments · 👍3 Every request returns stopReason: "length" with 16 output tokens and auto-compaction cannot recover. This is one of the highest-impact open bugs, affecting any long-running reasoning-model session. Link

  3. #10390 — Anthropic SSE parser mishandles CRLF split across chunks [OPEN] [bug] · 7 comments When \r and \n arrive in separate network chunks, the parser flushes an empty event and aborts the turn. A classic streaming edge case with outsized blast radius for Anthropic users. Link

  4. #11376 — Anthropic: removing an initial tool mid-session breaks all later requests [OPEN] [inprogress, prio:p0] · 4 comments Reloading an extension that stops registering a tool produces tool_reference_unresolved on every subsequent call. Highlights a gap between extension lifecycle and provider tool declaration state. Link

  5. #11460 — Resume drops all built-in tools when the session branch is truncated (orphan parentId after ENOSPC) [CLOSED] [prio:p0, fix-available] · 4 comments Disk-full conditions could leave the session graph with an orphan parent, silently removing read/bash/edit/... from resumed sessions. A serious data-integrity-style failure with a fix now available. Link

  6. #11415 — openai-responses: function_call items from other models replayed without namespace [CLOSED] [prio:p0] · 3 comments Tools declared via additional_tools caused OpenAI 400s because replayed calls lacked their namespace. Reproduced live by an agent against api.openai.com; a high-signal provider-compat fix. Link

  7. #11416 — Bedrock: request fails with more than 16 optional parameters [CLOSED] [prio:p0] · 2 comments Bedrock rejects schemas with >16 union/optional parameters, breaking otherwise valid tool definitions. Worth tracking because it imposes a hard tool-schema budget on Bedrock users. Link

  8. #11500 — Compaction/summarization requests share no prefix with live turns [CLOSED] [untriaged] · 2 comments Every compaction pays a full prefill because the summarizer starts from a fresh prompt without system prompt/tool declarations. Directly motivates PR #11499; big cost/latency implication for long sessions. Link

  9. #11493 — Codex: full cache miss after idle despite persistent-cache guarantee [CLOSED] [untriaged] · 2 comments Contradicts OpenAI's stated guarantee for logged-in Codex users, suggesting Pi may be altering request shape or identifiers across resumes. Cache behavior is a recurring cost concern for resumed sessions. Link

  10. #11433 — pi-env: exec hangs when a pipe-reader or waiter thread fails to start [OPEN] [bug] · 2 comments A thread-start failure (e.g., cgroup task limit) panics instead of returning an error, leaving the exec without a reply and cancellation broken. A rare but severe daemon-level hang. Link

Honorable mentions: #7738 (concurrent compactions share one AbortController → crash), #11497 (SqliteStorage ID minting across multiple openers), #11489 (pi update misdetects vite+ installs).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #11499 — feat(compaction): prefix-preserving summarization calls [CLOSED] Reworks summarization to pass the system prompt and tool declarations, replaying conversation as-is so compaction shares a token prefix with live turns. The direct fix for #11500 and the most consequential perf change of the day. Link

  2. #11498 — docs(coding-agent): restore the full extensions guide [CLOSED] Restores ~3,100 lines of extension API reference and tool guidance that a prior docs refresh cut down to 130 lines, corrected against current source. Important for the extension ecosystem. Link

  3. #11496 — fix(ai): cap OpenRouter reasoning tokens [CLOSED] Sends nested reasoning.max_tokens, omits reasoning.effort when a budget is present (OpenRouter rejects both), and clamps to preserve ≥1,024 answer tokens. Link

  4. #11494 — fix(ai): detect LiteLLM ContextWindowExceededError as context overflow [CLOSED] Recognizes LiteLLM's pre-call 400 (Max Input Tokens=…, Got=…) as overflow so auto-compaction can trigger instead of surfacing a raw provider error. Link

  5. #11491 — fix(coding-agent): detect vite+ global installs and self-update via vp [CLOSED] Adds a vite-plus install method so pi update stops creating a second divergent global install under vite+'s hash-keyed directory. Resolves #11489. Link

  6. #11434 — fix(ai): use OpenCode protocol-specific endpoints [CLOSED] Switches opencode / opencode-go traffic from the shared inference base to documented per-protocol endpoints (matching models.dev). Closes #11132. Link

  7. #11486 — fix(coding-agent): keep session memory in line with the file when a write fails [CLOSED] Prevents in-memory entries from being committed as the current leaf when the disk write fails (ENOSPC/EBUSY/ETIMEDOUT), avoiding orphaned parents on resume. Complements #11460. Link

  8. #11471 — feat(coding-agent): inline ctx.ui.custom() components report blocked program status [CLOSED] Lets custom dialogs opt into OSC 7501 blocked status (e.g., approval prompts), so terminals no longer show working while waiting on the user. Closes #11428. Link

  9. #11482 — fix(coding-agent): pass thinking level to branch summarization [CLOSED] /tree → Summarize was ignoring the session thinking level; reasoning is now included for OpenAI Responses/Azure reasoning models. Link

  10. #11487 — fix(tui): fall back to raw LaTeX when display math exceeds content width [CLOSED] Fixes broken multi-row math rendering where only the overflowing row wrapped and subsequent rows misaligned. Part of a broader TUI correctness push alongside #11422 (Kitty F-key decoding) and #11477 (scrollbar perf). Link

Also notable: #11348 (page-key support across all scrolling lists, still open) and #10528 (Nix packaging refactor, in progress).

5. Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #11488 — AY-PI: per-prompt tier routing and tool scoping (virtual model + Jev classifier) · 1 comment · 👍1 An extension demonstrating Pi's virtual model and classifier APIs: classifies each prompt into CHAT/SUGGEST/REVIEW/PLAN/CODE plus a low/medium/high tier, then scopes tools so only CODE keeps edit/write/bash. Link
  • #11476 — A Cairn-style shared board for coding agents (built for omp) · 👍1 Models problem-solving as state-space search over a shared board where agents coordinate via facts, intents, and hints; reports a 3rd-place finish in the Tencent Cloud AI Penetration Testing Challenge. Link

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Compaction & context economics — Requests center on making compaction cheaper and smarter: prefix-preserving summarization (#11500 / PR #11499), surfacing multiple context-window variants per model (#10893), and recovery from context-ceiling wedges (#9409).
  • Durable task orchestration — A steady stream of pi-durable requests: resume watchEvents from a last-seen ID (#11327), let extensions start tasks per turn (#11141), and let tasks hold the conversation busy (#11332).
  • Provider protocol fidelity — Multiple asks to match each provider's documented endpoints and error semantics: OpenCode protocol endpoints (#11132), LiteLLM overflow detection (#11494), OpenRouter reasoning budgets (#11496), and namespace-correct OpenAI Responses replay (#11415).
  • TUI interaction quality — Selection/copy semantics for soft wraps (#8019), configurable page keys honored everywhere (#11348), Kitty function-key decoding (#11422), and inline custom dialogs reporting blocked status (#11428).
  • Install/update correctness — Detect non-npm global installs (vite+, #11489) and suppress npm audit/fund noise during pi install (#11469).
  • Extension sandbox/authority clarity — Whether parent cancellation always propagates through ctx.executeTool() even with an explicit AbortSignal (#11484).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Sessions that cannot recover. The recurring theme is state integrity: wedging at the context ceiling (#9409), resume dropping built-in tools after a truncated branch (#11460), in-memory session state diverging from disk on write failure (#11486), and SqliteStorage ID collisions with multiple openers (#11497). Developers lose work or are forced to restart sessions.
  • Provider-specific fragility. Anthropic SSE chunk boundaries (#10390), unresolvable tool references after extension reload (#11376), Bedrock's 16-optional-parameter ceiling (#11416), and OpenAI Business auth policy denials (#10953) all present as opaque failures far from the root cause.
  • Cache and cost surprises. Full cache misses after idle on Codex (#11493) and full-prefill compactions (#11500) mean users pay significantly more than expected for resumed or long-running sessions.
  • Compaction/concurrency bugs. Concurrent compactions sharing a single AbortController (#7738) and durable generation infinite loops after host restart (#11139) indicate re-entrancy and lifecycle guards are still thin in critical paths.
  • Install/update ambiguity. Misdetected install methods (#11489) silently produce duplicate global installs, and npm's own advisory output (#11469) adds noise users can't safely act on.
  • Environment/daemon hangs. pi-env panicking on thread-start failure (#11433) leaves execs with no reply and broken cancellation — a low-frequency but hard-to-diagnose class of failure.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-10-28

1. Today's Highlights

Release cadence remains high: v0.26.2 shipped with a breaking change to Managed Agent Web Shell controls, followed by v0.26.3-preview.0 adding opt-in memory extraction cadence and XML tool-call recovery fixes. Meanwhile, two P1 correctness bugs landed in the tracker — a persistent Anthropic 400 caused by a thinking part with a missing signature, and a sed simulation mismatch in the shell tool. CI/release reliability continues to dominate discussion volume, with the Managed Agent gate issue at 68 comments and the dual-path architecture proposal at 72.

2. Releases

v0.26.3-preview.0

  • feat(memory): opt-in extraction cadence after a no-op run (#13571)
  • fix(core): recover outer XML calls with quoted candidates — continues the XML tool-call recovery work tracked in #13787

v0.26.2

  • Breaking: fix(managed-agent)! simplifies Web Shell controls and retires cwd submissions (#15616) — callers relying on cwd submission semantics must migrate.

v0.26.2-preview.1

  • feat(managed): session permission rules and Auto approval (#15448)
  • fix(cli): harden serve token resolution

sdk-typescript-v0.1.24

  • Bundles CLI 0.26.2 (built from the same branch/ref as the SDK). Note the release notes also reference a bundled 0.26.1, suggesting a skipped/renumbered cut.

Release-process note: v0.26.2-preview.0 publish failed (#15672, closed), and the fix is in review as PR #15730.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #15742 — P1: native Anthropic session 400s forever when a persisted thinking part lost its signature. A single assistant turn without thoughtSignature bricks the session with an unrecoverable invalid_request_error; there is no self-healing path. High severity for anyone on the native Anthropic endpoint.

  2. #15675 — P1: sed edit simulation diverges from real sed. The in-process simulation omits the s and u flags, so . fails to match \r and whole emoji. This is a correctness bug in the shell tool's fast path, not just a cosmetic mismatch.

  3. #12380 — proposal(serve): Managed Agent dual-path architecture and staged delivery. The highest-traffic issue in the window (72 comments), carrying a verified Stage F delivery status as of 2026-10-24. Effectively the design spine for the managed-agent roadmap.

  4. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified. 68 comments and autofix/skip, updated daily since 2026-10-19. Persistent "no test identified" failures are eroding trust in the gate as a signal.

  5. #15686 — P2: Active Goal blocks ordinary user input. Enter-steered messages and pasted text queue until the Goal leaves active state, contradicting the documented steering behavior. Six comments already; a UX/state-machine conflict rather than a simple bug.

  6. #15741 — P2: MCP duplicate tool names discard the entire server. One collision silently drops every tool from that server and reports a misleading "no tools" error. Reproduced with a Unity MCP server on 0.26.2.

  7. #15738 — P2: team-mode messages never reach the leader in ACP mode. With qwen serve --web and experimental.agentTeam, no teammate message is delivered and the team dies with the short-lived --acp child. Blocks the multi-agent story in Web Shell.

  8. #15690 — P2: Homebrew 0.26.1 cannot rewrite libopentui.dylib install name. @opentui/core-darwin-arm64 lacks -headerpad_max_install_names, so brew upgrade emits a linkage error on Apple Silicon. Packaging-level breakage for macOS users.

  9. #15645 — P2: daemon skills catalog stays stale after on-disk skill creation. The runtime skills endpoint sees the new project skill but the configuration endpoint does not — a split-brain that will confuse management UIs.

  10. #15697 — P2: web-shell history-viewport smoke test burns its 120s budget. Same spec and assertion failing across two unrelated PRs that don't touch packages/web-shell/. Concrete flake data makes this one actionable.

Also notable: #13024 (IO Intelligence provider preset) is the only issue in the set with meaningful positive reaction at 10 👍; #13078 (dependency CVE audit failure, 33 comments) remains open and needs triage; #15499 tracks the managed-runtime v0.26.1 preflight stop.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #15745 — feat(managed): independent worktrees for main sessions. Managed main Sessions can opt into a per-session Git worktree; admission freezes a local commit and records the working directory before Runtime start. The enabling primitive for parallel managed work.

  2. #15730 — fix(release): use the job token for the publish checkout. Directly targets the publish-stage release failures, keeping the PAT only on the branch push and GitHub release steps.

  3. #15746 — fix(verify-pr): bind reports to their round snapshot. Prevents a newer verification round in another artifact directory from retroactively changing how an earlier report is evaluated. Review-integrity fix.

  4. #15388 — feat(ci): bound autofix takeover with a round budget. @qwen-code /takeover for N (1–99) records a window-scoped round budget. Addresses the "autofix never converges" failure mode.

  5. #15435 — feat(web-shell): show tool arguments and results in expanded cards. Expanded tool cards now render call arguments and full results for tools without a built-in detail view; JSON is pretty-printed. Meaningful transparency improvement in the transcript.

  6. #14613 — feat(cli): enable LSP through a user-scoped setting and env pair. Makes the experimental LSP code-intelligence service reachable without a CLI flag; the disable switch takes precedence over enable.

  7. #15681 — fix(core): don't treat fd duplication (2>&1) as a file write. Fixes false-positive permission prompts for a very common shell idiom.

  8. #14670 — fix(core): split shell commands on bash's separators, not JS whitespace. /\s/ matches characters bash treats as ordinary word characters (\r, \v, \f, \u00a0), which could mis-split commands used in permission analysis.

  9. #14677 — fix(core): treat a reassigned HOME as dynamic for cd and ~. Closes a permission-analysis hole where HOME=/x; cd was certified against the wrong path.

  10. #15358 — fix(cli): report max session turns in JSON result instead of replaying the last answer. BaseJsonOutputAdapter now latches MaxSessionTurns and emits a real error rather than a false success. Important for CI consumers parsing JSON output.

Related in flight: the sdk-java lock-scoping series (#15274, #15275, #15286) converges on the same design — seed a job-local Maven repo, hold the host lock only for cache write-back. Consolidating them would reduce review load.

5. Hot Discussions

No GitHub Discussions data was provided for this window, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Provider preset expansion and compatibility. #13024 (io.net preset, 10 👍) and #12072 (X-OpenRouter-Title vs X-Title) point at a steady demand for first-class presets plus correct vendor-specific headers.
  • Managed Agent / multi-agent maturity. Dual-path architecture (#12380), independent session worktrees (#15745), session permission rules (#15448), and team-mode delivery in ACP (#15738). This is the largest coherent feature cluster.
  • Web Shell interaction design. Archived conversations out of the persistent sidebar (#15549), a configurable simple input mode (#15647), composer polish (#15691), and tool-card detail (#15435).
  • Context and token management. Dynamic tool-output truncation under context pressure (#2566) and memory extraction cadence (#13571) are both about spending context deliberately rather than reactively.
  • Shell-tool fidelity and permission correctness. sed simulation parity (#15675), fd duplication (#15681), bash word splitting (#14670), and HOME reassignment (#14677) form a clear sub-theme: emulate bash exactly, or don't emulate it at all.
  • Release/CI self-hosting. Provisioning a release-only host on the idle ARM64 pool (#15461) and per-SHA E2E validation (#15052).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI signal is noisy and expensive to interpret. At least five concurrent CI-related threads this window: #14724 (68 comments, no test identified), #14796 (Install dependencies failing before any test), #15697 (timeout flake), #15677 (5 of 6 failing on darwin-x64), and #15052 (replaced pending runs). Contributors are spending review bandwidth triaging infra rather than code.
  • The release pipeline stops at publish. #15499 (immutable-publication preflight), #15672 (preview publish failure), and #15461 (publish competing for GitHub-hosted capacity) describe one systemic bottleneck: publish is the last job without dedicated capacity.
  • Shell emulation edge cases cause both false approvals and false prompts. The sed regex flag gap, /\s/ vs bash separators, HOME reassignment, and 2>&1 as a "write" all stem from approximating a shell in JavaScript. Each fix is small; the class of bug is not.
  • Persistent, unrecoverable session state failures. #15742 (missing thoughtSignature → permanent 400) and #15645 (stale skills catalog) both leave users with a session they cannot repair without manual intervention.
  • "Deferred review findings" is accumulating as a backlog pattern. #13268, #11056, #15674, #15707, and #15527 are all ledgers created because PRs exceeded review-round or size ceilings. The 1500-addition patrol rule works, but the deferred work has no owner.
  • macOS distribution remains fragile. #15690 (missing -headerpad_max_install_names in @opentui/core-darwin-arm64) is a dependency-ownership gap that breaks Homebrew upgrades for every Apple Silicon user on 0.26.1.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw 生态日报 2026-10-28

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-10-28 01:35 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目摘要 — 2026-10-28

1. 今日概览

截至 2026-10-28，OpenClaw 展现出极高吞吐：过去 24 小时有 500 个 issue 和 500 个 PR 更新，其中 391 个活跃 issue、109 个已关闭 issue、275 个开放 PR、225 个已合并/关闭 PR。三个版本分别落地到 beta、非 beta 和 extended-stable 通道，表明发布工程活跃。然而，issue 构成严重偏向生产稳定性：在前 50 个抽样中至少出现 9 个开放 P0 issue，涵盖 Gateway 事件循环阻塞、Windows/更新失败、会话/DB 恢复以及 memory 引导。整体健康度喜忧参半：贡献者/维护者吞吐强劲且社区复现活跃，但稳定性风险偏高，因为若干高评论数 P0/P1 issue 仍没有可见的修复 PR。

2. 发布

过去 24 小时发布了三个新版本：

  • v2026.10.10-beta.4 — Beta 版本。主要声明修复：自动化在显式的同一会话定时后续操作中保留已认证操作员权限，包括一次性 next_check 重新激活，同时保留角色、会话、取消、目标和工具策略的撤销边界。提供的说明中未声明破坏性变更或迁移步骤。
  • v2026.10.8 — 聚焦更新恢复的版本。声明修复包括：普通更新后 Doctor 失败时重启 Gateway，而不是让其保持停止状态；防止孤立的维护 worker 阻塞 CLI 命令和 Gateway 启动；避免在 ACL 文件系统和 Windows 相关更新路径上中止更新。未明确声明破坏性变更或迁移说明。
  • v2026.9.35 — 仅 Gateway 的 extended-stable 版本，被描述为当前 LTS 等效版本。它基于 2026 年 9 月底的 OpenClaw，加上关键安全更新、可靠性/性能修复和新模型支持。

迁移/破坏性变更评估： 提供的发布说明中未列出破坏性变更或显式迁移步骤。对于要从更新后 Gateway 失败状态中恢复的运维人员，v2026.10.8 是最相关的版本；v2026.9.35 是保守的 extended-stable 通道。

3. 项目进展

过去 24 小时，225 个 PR 已合并/关闭，275 个仍开放。样本显示在安全边界、更新/重启可靠性、会话恢复、可访问性和平台特定修复方面均有进展。

样本中已关闭/合并 PR 信号：

  • PR #186417 — 已关闭的安全修复：webhook、mapped-hook、plugin-trigger 和 join-introduction 轮次不再使用 owner-only 工具运行。
  • PR #183018 — 已关闭的 UI 修复：将访客访问指引保留在 Profile 中，同时避免 Inbox 中出现误导性警告。
  • PR #178347 — 已关闭的文档修复：澄清基于镜像的主机在升级后若在 Doctor 运行前持续宕机，如何恢复。

推进项目的重要开放/就绪 PR：

  • PR #185730 — 大型重构：在优雅重启后恢复正在运行的会话，减少长时间重启排空和恢复争用。
  • PR #185939 — 从并发追加中恢复 transcript 重写，针对会话/transcript 完整性。
  • PR #186420 和 PR #186426 — 改进配额类 429 时的模型回退行为，而不是在固定模型或同 profile 认证轮换上走入死胡同。
  • PR #186415 — 防止打开的 node skill 监视将 Gateway 重启推迟满 300 秒。
  • PR #186411 — 修复更新清理未通过其自身目标检查的问题。
  • PR #185921 — 添加 TUI 屏幕阅读器模式；若合并，将关闭可访问性 issue #9637。
  • PR #186416 — 恢复多 agent Gateway 上的 iOS 图片分享。
  • PR #185028 — 在浏览器导航防护中保留原生 CORS 预检请求。
  • PR #184524 — 修复流式回复引用空命令输出时二次方级重复扫描的问题。
  • PR #184712 — 压缩连续的 Telegram 进度工具调用，以保持预览有用。

样本中已关闭 issue 信号： 重复 transcript 写入（#118185）、两个文件后 memory 索引停滞（#130955）、计费冷却恢复请求（#115642）、原生 Codex 中止作用域完成失败（#167410）、memory 索引 SIGTERM 孤儿问题（#185902），以及更新失败报告（#169937、#153094）。

4. 社区热门话题

提供的 PR 评论数为空，因此下面热门话题排名使用 issue 评论数。反应数总体较低；样本中最明显的支持是 #7722 的 4 个 👍。

  • #160959 — 58 条评论，P0。 Gateway 在捕获大型外部/工作区插件时阻塞数分钟，这是 2026.9.6 的回归。底层需求： 插件捕获隔离、流式限制或异步准备，使 Gateway 启动和运行时重新发布不会耗尽事件循环。
  • #119720 — 25 条评论，P1。 同步 agent 持久化和 transcript 维护在规模化时阻塞 Gateway 事件循环。底层需求： 异步持久化、背压以及有界的 transcript 维护工作。
  • #170956 — 22 条评论，P0。 Windows 托管服务安装表现为启动缓慢、插件关闭不干净以及 schtasks 权限错误，使重启/更新不可靠。底层需求： 更强的 Windows 服务生命周期处理和更新恢复。
  • #157325 — 19 条评论，P0。 卡住的 agent-DB 资源会使每个 agent 的回复都失败，直到 Gateway 重启。底层需求： DB 资源健康检查、自动恢复以及按 agent 隔离故障。
  • #120385 — 18 条评论，P2。 Code Mode 工具目录对定时/cron 和 memory-flush 轮次不完整，导致 “Unknown tool id” 失败。底层需求： 在所有轮次类型中保持一致的工具发现和目录构建。
  • 次级高互动 issue：#166634（15 条评论，P0 回收检查点失败）、#121953（14 条评论，P1 DeepSeek cron 前缀停滞）、#177656（14 条评论，P1 共享状态完整性错误），以及 #172837（14 条评论，P1 Codex 原生子 agent 分配未移除）。

5. 缺陷与稳定性

前 50 个样本中的 P0 issue——最高严重性：

  • #160959 — Gateway 事件循环在大型插件捕获时阻塞数分钟。提供的标签中未看到新的修复 PR。
  • #170956 — Windows 启动缓慢、插件关闭不干净以及 schtasks 权限错误。未看到新的修复 PR。
  • #157325 — 卡住的 agent-DB 资源导致所有 agent 回复失败，直到重启。标记为 needs-live-repro。
  • #166634 — 晚期回收检查点失败导致 agent 在崩溃恢复后不可用。标记为 not-repro-on-main。
  • #161921 — state-migrated-no-rollback 使 doctor --fix 和 plugins update 相互阻塞。未看到新的修复 PR。
  • #167406 — Windows MSIX 启用 Codex 的 Gateway 启动耗尽主线程。未看到修复 PR。
  • #185819 — Windows 快速启动中的 Codex 入门流程完成设备认证，但因 harness 运行时制品未激活而激活失败。未看到修复 PR。
  • #164800 — 从 2026.9.7 到 2026.9.8 的托管更新使激活驱动失效，直到主机重启。未看到修复 PR。
  • #158912 — 尽管文档如此，MEMORY.md 在 2026.9.6 的引导时不再注入。未看到修复 PR。

部分 P1 稳定性 issue：

  • #119720 — 同步持久化/transcript 维护阻塞事件循环。
  • #117262 — 来自三个并发写句柄的 SQLite 争用导致约 33 秒事件循环停顿。
  • #121953 — 由于 [cron:...] 前缀，cron agent 轮次在 DeepSeek 上停滞。
  • #177656 — 原生主机 exec 返回共享状态完整性准入错误，且无子进程结果。
  • #172837 — Codex 原生子 agent 分配在完成投递放弃后从未移除。
  • #181432 — 2026.10.5 中基线 RSS 过高（约 1.9 GB）且 SQLite 事务超时。
  • #166017 — MCP 会话空闲 TTL 默认值未应用；spawn broker 达到 256 个子进程硬上限。有关联的开放 PR。
  • #169797 — 单 CPU 主机上 Gateway 内存回归以及启动/首条回复变慢。
  • #181078 — Agent 轮次间歇性失败，报 “Canonical session reader continuation is no longer current.”
  • #184720 — Windows 中断更新修复留下空的 Doctor 保管回执。
  • #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive 在插件捕获阶段空转 15 分钟以上。
  • #118776 — 叶子子 agent 保留 sessions_yield，但丢失了本可产生所等待事件的工具。
  • #166964 — 当请求方权限被撤销时，子 agent 完成投递永久失败。

修复 PR 可见性： 评论数最高的 P0——#160959、#170956、#161921、#164800 和 #185819——在提供的标签中未显示可见修复 PR。相邻领域存在相关开放 PR：transcript 重写恢复（#185939）、模型回退（#186420、#186426）、重启推迟（#186415）、更新清理（#186411）、浏览器 CORS（#185028），以及 iOS 图片分享（#186416）。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

  • #7722 — 文件系统沙箱配置（tools.fileAccess），支持允许/拒绝路径。安全敏感，4 个 👍，已标记供产品和安全审查。重要，但若无明确安全设计不太可能落地。
  • #13219 — 按模型的使用量日志，用于成本跟踪。运维需求明确；目前用户必须手动解析 session JSONL。
  • #9637 — 禁用 TUI 中 emoji/unicode 的可访问性选项。已有开放实现 PR：#185921 添加屏幕阅读器模式，使其成为较可能近期落地的 UX 改进之一。
  • #52732 — 在 agents.list 中按 agent 覆盖 compaction 和 contextPruning。需要产品决策；与多 agent 部署相关。
  • #175826 — Android 在聊天内可选问题和原生审批请求方面的功能对齐。需要在实现前完成设计验收。
  • #172547 — 从 memory-search 索引和召回信号中排除围栏式 dreaming 范围。需要围绕 memory 语义做出产品决策。
  • #184600 — Skill Workshop 未经用户审查/同意自动变更技能。这既是缺陷/UX 问题，也是治理/安全路线图信号。

基于开放 PR 的可能下一版本候选： TUI 屏幕阅读器模式（#185921）、模型回退/配额处理（#186420、#186426）、重启/更新可靠性（#186415、#186411），以及会话续跑/恢复工作（#185730、#185939）。沙箱、按 agent 修剪和 Android 审批对齐看起来更依赖产品/安全决策。

7. 用户反馈摘要

主要痛点： 生产可靠性和升级安全。用户报告插件捕获和持久化导致 Gateway 事件循环停顿（#160959、#119720、#117262）；Windows 服务/更新失败（#170956、#164800、#184720、#185819）；以及更新/Doctor/插件死锁（#161921）。

会话与消息完整性： 反复报告 agent DB 状态卡住（#157325）、回收检查点失败（#166634）、canonical 会话读取器错误（#181078）、重复 transcript 写入（#118185，已关闭），以及子 agent 完成投递失败（#166964）。

Memory/索引： 缺少 MEMORY.md 引导（#158912）、重建索引锁阻止修复并累积 19 GB 临时 DB（#136311）、全量索引发布耗尽 SQLite busy timeout（#143640）、memory 膨胀回归（#181432、#169797），以及 dreaming ranker/applier 不匹配（#121232）。

安全/治理与 UX： 向 hook/join-introduction 轮次暴露 owner-only 工具的问题已在 #186417 中修复；用户仍然要求文件系统沙箱（#7722）和 Skill Workshop 自动变更的治理（#184600）。UX 摩擦包括 Control UI transcript 抖动（#164394）、webchat 通知错位（#177094）、掩码配置值导致故障误诊（#173313）、Telegram 进度预览拥挤（#184712），以及可访问性缺口（#9637、#185921）。

情绪评估： 未提供调查数据，但 issue 情绪在生产稳定性和升级方面较为紧张。积极信号包括社区积极复现、详细的运维报告、关联 PR 和维护者分诊标签；不满集中在反复出现的 P0/P1 可靠性失败，以及回滚/诊断路径不足。

8. 积压项观察

这些条目陈旧或影响重大、讨论较多，且仍需维护者关注：

  • #160959 — 自 2026-09-29 起为 P0，58 条评论，无新修复 PR。最高优先级的 Gateway 事件循环阻塞项。
  • #119720 — 自 2026-08-05 起为 P1，25 条评论，无新修复 PR。长期存在的持久化/事件循环扩展问题。
  • #117262 — 自 2026-08-01 起为 P1，12 条评论。SQLite 写句柄争用导致约 33 秒停顿。
  • #121953 — 自 2026-08-11 起为 P1，14 条评论。DeepSeek cron 前缀停滞仍未解决。
  • #136311 — 自 2026-09-02 起为 P2，12 条评论。Memory 重建索引锁和孤立临时 DB 累积。
  • #161921 — 自 2026-09-30 起为 P0，11 条评论，无新修复 PR。更新/Doctor/插件死锁阻塞恢复。
  • #170956 — 自 2026-10-13 起为 P0，22 条评论，无新修复 PR。Windows 重启/更新可靠性。
  • #7722 — 自 2026-02-03 起为 P2 安全增强，11 条评论，4 个 👍。文件系统沙箱配置需要产品/安全决策。
  • #13219 — 自 2026-02-10 起为 P2，9 条评论。用于成本跟踪的按模型使用量日志。
  • #52732 — 自 2026-03-23 起为 P2，7 条评论。按 agent 的 compaction/context-pruning 覆盖需要产品决策。

PR 积压说明： 样本中的大多数高影响力 PR 都是近期的。最明显的较旧 PR 是 #156626，这是一个仅测试的 relay 匹配重构，自 2026-09-23 起开放并等待作者；相对于 P0/P1 issue 积压，其产品风险较低。

横向生态对比

1. 生态系统概览

2026-10-28，个人 AI 助手/代理开源格局正围绕网关/运行时核心、多端客户端（桌面、Web、移动端、消息平台）以及 MCP/工具集成收敛。活动量很高但不均衡：OpenClaw 处于超大规模运营，Hermes Agent、QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw 在 22–50 个 issue/PR 区间迭代，而 IronClaw 在本窗口期不活跃。发布工程正成为差异化因素——OpenClaw 发布了三个通道，QwenPaw 发布了一个 beta，ZeroClaw 发布了一个安全补丁，而 Hermes 没有发布。共同拖累不再是功能广度，而是生产环境加固：会话身份、异步运行时健康、供应商兼容性、MCP 可靠性和 principal 感知的安全。

2. 活动对比

计数为 24 小时更新/触及数，并非仓库总数。健康度* 是分析人员结合活跃度、发布节奏、稳定性/安全性和评审吞吐的启发式指标；它不是上游项目指标。

项目 Issue 数（24 小时） PR 数（24 小时） 发布状态 健康度*
OpenClaw 500 更新：391 开启/活跃，109 已关闭 500 更新：275 开启，225 已合并/关闭 3 个发布：beta、更新恢复稳定版、扩展稳定 LTS 6.5/10 — 吞吐量高，P0 风险偏高
Hermes Agent 50 触及：47 开启，3 已关闭 50 触及：43 开启，7 已合并/关闭 无发布；用户参考 v0.22.5 稳定版 5.8/10 — 分诊量大，会话架构债务
IronClaw 无活动 无活动 无发布 N/A — 窗口期不活跃
QwenPaw 36 触及：16 开启，20 已关闭 50 触及：39 开启，11 已合并/关闭 v2.3.0-beta.1 7.0/10 — 响应及时，评审积压
ZeroClaw 22 更新：21 开启，1 已关闭 42 更新：41 开启，1 已合并/关闭 v0.8.7 安全/维护版 6.7/10 — 发布纪律好，安全/评审瓶颈

3. OpenClaw 的定位

相较同行的优势。 OpenClaw 以数量级优势领先规模：24 小时内触及 500 个 issue 和 500 个 PR，其中 225 个 PR 已合并/关闭——相比之下 Hermes 为 7，QwenPaw 为 11，ZeroClaw 为 1。它也是本组中唯一拥有三个活跃发布通道的项目，其中包括一个等同于 LTS 的扩展稳定通道。其 issue 互动深度为样本中最高：排名第一的 Gateway 事件循环 issue 有 58 条评论，而 Hermes 的头号条目为 24 条，ZeroClaw 为 16 条，QwenPaw 为 5 条。

技术路线差异。 OpenClaw 是一个横向的、以 Gateway 为中心的平台：会话、插件、通道、Doctor/更新恢复和安全边界都集中在一个明显对事件循环阻塞敏感的运行时中。同行更聚焦、更纵向：Hermes 正在构建规范化的多端会话/协议层；QwenPaw 集中于桌面/控制台上下文、记忆、MCP 和供应商兼容性；ZeroClaw 以安全为先，采用 OIDC、principal 作用域以及 Rust/Tokio/Wasmtime 风格的技术栈。OpenClaw 的优势在于广度和运维工具；风险在于同一个中心化运行时集中了生产稳定性故障。

社区规模对比。 OpenClaw 的吞吐量不仅更大——它处在不同的运营层级。它在 24 小时内关闭/合并了 225 个 PR，约为 Hermes、QwenPaw 和 ZeroClaw 可见合并吞吐量的 20–30 倍。这意味着大得多的贡献者/维护者基数和更多生产部署面，但也带来更难的分诊问题：前 50 个样本中至少出现九个开启的 P0，且若干头部 P0 缺少可见修复 PR。

4. 共同技术关注领域

共同需求 涉及项目 具体要求
会话持久化、恢复与身份 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw 跨重启和跨端可恢复会话；显式所有权，而非基于 source 的锁定；从对话记录/DB 损坏中恢复；仅追加的事件历史；会话加载/恢复 API。
异步运行时健康与背压 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw 非阻塞持久化和插件捕获；有界队列；SQLite 争用控制；网关停滞检测；按 profile 的线程/资源限制；MCP 连接恢复。
供应商/模型兼容性与成本感知回退 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw 配额感知的 429 回退；如 thinking-disable 请求形态等传输格式的特殊行为；OAuth/订阅登录；Codex 流式行为；模型目录漂移；类型化供应商错误。
MCP/工具协议与工具调用完整性 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw 旧版 MCP 协商回退；中毒会话恢复；每轮一致的工具目录；schema/参数校验；审批路径安全；principal 感知的工具选择器。
安全、治理与最小权限 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw 文件系统沙箱；审计日志完整性；OIDC/SSO；CSP；仅所有者可用的工具边界；审批允许列表加固；防止子代理/插件权限提升。
升级/安装可靠性与多端一致性 OpenClaw、Hermes、QwenPaw、ZeroClaw 自愈更新与回滚；Windows/Android 安装稳健性；保留故障原因的诊断信息；移动端键盘/输入；PWA/Linux 打包；无障碍模式。

IronClaw 在本窗口期没有数据，未纳入共同需求证据。

5. 差异化分析

项目 主要功能重点 目标用户 架构/路线
OpenClaw 广泛的网关/插件平台、多渠道运营、更新恢复、LTS 运维人员、高级用户、生产级多渠道部署 以 Gateway 为中心的核心；插件/通道；Doctor/更新路径；扩展稳定发布通道；对事件循环敏感的运行时。
Hermes Agent 多端对话连续性与客户端协议 高级用户、远程 hermes serve 部署、第三方客户端构建者 规范化会话权威 + 网关；Desktop/Webapp/mobile/TUI 多端；profile 多路复用；当前正在偿还会话所有权债务。
QwenPaw 桌面/控制台代理工作区、上下文压缩、记忆、MCP/供应商广度、治理 需要 MCP、记忆、审计和供应商灵活性的桌面及企业用户 基于 Python 的控制台/桌面技术栈；技能/通道/插件；SQLite 历史；模型注册表；治理审计；Windows/Linux 打包。
ZeroClaw 安全优先的自托管网关/仪表盘、身份/访问、运行时加固 重视安全的自托管用户和企业风格部署 Rust/Tokio/Wasmtime 技术栈；网关/仪表盘；OIDC 与 principal 作用域；仅追加会话历史；v0.9.0 聚焦运行时/网关。
IronClaw 窗口期内无可见活动 未知 根据所给数据未知。

OpenClaw 是横向平台型打法。Hermes 是多端连续性打法。QwenPaw 是桌面/上下文/供应商兼容性打法。ZeroClaw 是安全/身份打法。这种差异化是健康的，但四者都在收敛到相同的运维要求：重启安全的会话、异步运行时隔离、供应商抽象、MCP 稳健性和最小权限工具访问。

6. 社区动能与成熟度

第一梯队——超大规模、发布工程化： OpenClaw。活动量遥遥领先，24 小时内 225 个 PR 已合并/关闭，三次发布（包括一个等同 LTS 的版本）。它迭代迅速，但成熟度不均衡：强大的发布工程和社区复现能力，与多个 P0 稳定性问题以及头部阻塞项缺少可见修复 PR 并存。

第二梯队——高速稳定器： QwenPaw、ZeroClaw 和 Hermes Agent。

  • QwenPaw 是样本中响应最快的修复者：关闭 20 个 issue，合并/关闭 11 个 PR，并有若干同日/近日的 issue→PR 配对。其约束是评审带宽，有 39 个开启 PR 和若干持续数周的 size/XXXL 工作。
  • ZeroClaw 发布纪律强——v0.8.7 包含来自 19 位贡献者的 81 次提交——以及清晰的 v0.9.0 安全/身份主题。瓶颈是评审/安全分诊：41 个开启 PR 对 1 个已合并/关闭，且若干安全发现尚无修复 PR。
  • Hermes Agent 分诊重而非合并重：47 个开启 issue，43 个开启 PR，7 个已合并/关闭，无发布。Webapp 合并后余震和会话所有权集群表明，它正在架构债务下趋于稳定，而不是交付净新增面。

第三梯队——窗口期不活跃： IronClaw 在过去 24 小时没有活动；无法根据本摘要判断动能或成熟度。

7. 趋势信号

行业趋势 来自社区反馈的证据 对 AI 代理开发者的价值
会话连续性正在成为产品本身 Hermes 的头号 issue 是 Desktop/mobile/Webapp/TUI 上“列出但无法打开”的会话；OpenClaw 有重启/会话/DB 恢复工作；ZeroClaw 在重新加载时丢失提示词；QwenPaw 会话在切换供应商后损坏。 尽早设计会话身份、所有权和可恢复事件日志。将“跨端、跨重启的一段对话”视为核心契约，而非 UI 功能。
可靠性如今是功能，而非运维事后补充 OpenClaw 事件循环阻塞、SQLite 停滞、更新/Doctor 死锁；Hermes 网关在负载下停滞；QwenPaw 压缩中止；ZeroClaw 中毒 MCP 会话。 从第一天起，将异步持久化、有界队列、健康检查、回滚路径和诊断保留构建进运行时。
供应商抽象必须基于能力，而非模型名称 OpenClaw 配额感知回退；QwenPaw 禁用 thinking/传输格式怪癖；ZeroClaw Codex 流式与推理强度；Hermes ChatGPT 登录供应商。 实现类型化供应商能力、配额感知回退、OAuth/订阅认证，以及按供应商的错误归一化。
MCP/工具互操作性是集成战场 QwenPaw 旧版 MCP 协商失败；ZeroClaw 中毒 MCP 会话和过期套接字；OpenClaw 工具目录缺口和 MCP 启动上限；Hermes 工具参数 schema 失败。 投资于 MCP 协商回退、会话恢复、schema 校验，以及跨轮次类型的一致工具发现。
安全正在左移到代理运行时 ZeroClaw 的 OIDC/XFF/SOP/principal 作用域发现；OpenClaw 沙箱与所有者工具修复；Hermes 审批允许列表绕过；QwenPaw 审计日志完整性和工作区外写入。 采用 principal 感知的工具访问、审计轨迹、沙箱、CSP，以及面向插件、钩子、子代理和消息端的安全默认值。
多端一致性和无障碍正在成为基线期望 Hermes 移动端键盘/视口问题；OpenClaw TUI 屏幕阅读器模式和 iOS 分享；QwenPaw Windows/Linux 打包；ZeroClaw Android shell 失败。 在客户端之间共享一套协议，但要为移动端输入、视口、无障碍、打包和平台特定生命周期行为预留预算。
维护者评审带宽是扩展约束 QwenPaw 的 39 个开启 PR 和持续数周的 XXXL 工作；ZeroClaw 的 41 个开启 PR；Hermes 的 43:7 开启对已合并比例；OpenClaw 中缺少可见修复 PR 的 P0。 当项目达到中等规模后，模块化所有权、大型变更的设计文档门禁和分诊自动化，与贡献者增长同样重要。

结论： 生态系统正从“代理演示”走向“代理基础设施”。赢家将是那些让会话可移植、运行时非阻塞、供应商可互换、MCP 可恢复、权限可审计——同时不牺牲多端可用性或发布速度的项目。

Hermes Agent — 项目摘要

1. 今日概览

Hermes Agent 正处于深度稳定化阶段：过去 24 小时内共有 100 个 issue 和 PR 被处理（50 个 issue——47 个开放 / 3 个已关闭；50 个 PR——43 个开放 / 7 个已合并或关闭），无新版本发布。活动绝大多数是入站缺陷分诊而非功能交付——开放与合并比（43:7）反映出维护者队列的积压速度快于消化速度。最主要的信号是浏览器托管 Webapp（#141864，2026-10-25 合并）合并后的余震，目前已有专门的跟踪 issue（#144648）和多个子 PR 在进行中。贯穿整份报告的第二个更大的结构性主题是：会话身份、归属和跨界面恢复在多个不同层面上出现故障，这表明问题出在规范会话权威的架构缺口，而非一组孤立缺陷。整体健康度读作高速度但承压——分诊纪律良好（严重性标签、组件标签、sweeper:risk-* 标记），但 P2 积压不断增长，相应的修复 PR 却寥寥无几。

4. 社区热点话题

1. #139818 — 24 条评论，👍2 · 远程后端桌面会话无法恢复 （P2，sweeper:risk-session-state） Hermes Desktop 针对远程 hermes serve 后端创建的对话以 source='desktop' 持久化，但一旦托管进程重启，session.resume 返回 not_found。这是窗口期内讨论最多的单项，也是下文会话身份集群的核心。

2. #144648 — 10 条评论 · 跟踪：Webapp 合并后后续工作 （type/security，P2） 维护者拥有的 #141864 总括 issue。明确将 Webapp 定位为跨浏览器标签页、CLI、原生 Desktop 和消息共享一个网关——"每个界面看到的是同一段对话"。子工作已可见：#145788（移动端标签页选择器菜单）、#145573（Webapp 页面的 CSP，WA-11）、#145803（Android insertText）。

3. #112028 — 8 条评论，👍1 · 多界面访问同一会话 （P2，needs-decision） 服务器拒绝第二个界面（移动端仪表盘）写入已在 Desktop 上打开的会话。这是对多界面需求最古老、最明确的表述。

4. #144814 — 7 条评论，👍1 · hermes-mobile 会话永远无法从原生 Desktop 恢复 对话记录在侧边栏中渲染，但打开时失败，报错 JsonRpcGatewayError: not_found。同一根因，不同客户端配对。

5. #141854 — 6 条评论 · 消息页面永远显示"Needs setup" 配置文件作用域的 _platform_enablement 要求必填环境变量，因此无令牌平台（WhatsApp、webhook、A2A）始终报告 configured: false。

底层需求分析： 五个最热条目中有四个描述的是同一个用户期望——一段对话，可在任何设备或界面上访问，归属同一身份。当前实现将 source/login 视为归属戳记，因此由 desktop、hermes-mobile、ios 或仪表盘 basic-auth 登录写入的会话在其他地方可见但不可打开。用户不将其理解为权限模型，而是数据丢失。相关：#145074（"一个人，多个登录"——聊天记录被分割到不可见的用户中）和 #143831（0.22.4 回归永久孤立遗留自定义 source 标签）。这是看板上杠杆率最高的架构决策。

数据中可见的满意度驱动因素： 用户正在运行真正苛刻的工作负载——多配置文件网关（出现 3 和 28 个配置文件安装）、负载 30–100 的 macOS 主机、200+ 网关线程、cron 链、看板工作器集群、basic auth 后面的远程 hermes serve，以及基于协议构建的第三方移动客户端（Hy4ri 的 Android 客户端、iOS "Cadu" 客户端）。人们正在针对 Hermes 构建客户端这一事实是强烈的生态系统信号。

不满意 / 痛点，按数量排序：

  1. "我的对话消失了。" 最主要的抱怨。会话被列出但无法打开，多份报告指出失败是静默的（TUI 启动新会话；Desktop 发送被取消且无提示）。即使用户行存在，用户也将其感知为数据丢失。
  2. 不透明的失败消息。 #143874（"每次票据失败都读作同一字符串"）、#145286（策略拒绝被渲染为模型连接错误）和 #143561 都描述了同样的挫败感：系统知道为什么失败，却在上一行将其丢弃。
  3. Windows 和负载主机上的运维脆弱性。 陈旧的 gateway.pid 每次运行都破坏 hermes update，加上负载下的网关超时，今天都已关闭——但这正是驱使

7. 用户反馈摘要

痛点，按频率排列：

  1. 长会话会坏。 压缩（#8312、#8417、#5856）、会话卡死（#7966、#8290）和无法恢复的超时（#7935）占主导。用户反复指出这些并非新问题——在 2.2.x 及更早版本中就有报告。
  2. Provider 兼容性脆弱。 严格兼容的端点会拒绝重复或无法识别的参数（#8417、#8436）；provider 切换会使历史记录失效（#7966）；模型目录漂移（#8447）。
  3. MCP 是集成战场。 UI（#8405）和协议协商（#8424、#8047）的失败方式都会静默地将服务器置为 inactive，并伴随 Console 503。
  4. 企业/治理缺口。 审计日志静默失效（#8412）和工作区外写入绕过（#7727）正是受监管用户无法容忍的故障。
  5. 防护栏过度触发。 自终止检测（#8413）会阻止合法的 kill $PID；长文件名会因原子写入的临时命名而被拒绝（#8306）。
  6. Windows 桌面仍是二等公民。 日志轮转（#8185）、安装器诊断（#8455）、响应消失（#3281）和 CSP 字体阻止（#8458）都集中在这里。
  7. 成本/访问摩擦。 OAuth/Codex 的一组讨论串是最清晰的“我想使用现有订阅”信号。

满意度信号： 快速周转可见——#8415 于 10-25 报告，修复 PR #8433 于 10-26 提交；#8361 → #8457；#8417 → #8436。报告者提交了包含 commit hash 的详细复现，表明用户群体参与度高且技术成熟。

潜在需求： 最热门的讨论集中在（1）发布工程简化（#9101），（2）协调 v0.9.0 运行时/网关规划（#7432），以及（3）安全/身份访问正确性（#11913、#11961、#12047）。PR 评论数不可用，但诸如 #11921 和 #9745 这样的大型/高风险 PR 很可能是评审瓶颈。

5. Bug 与稳定性

S1 — 工作流受阻

Issue 状态 / 修复
#10807 — 一次恢复尝试失败导致 MCP 连接被永久污染（p1，risk:high） 修复 PR #12061 已打开。
#12075 — Android shell 工具始终失败；/system/bin/sh 规范化 EPERM 修复 PR #12080 已打开。

S2 — 行为降级

Issue 状态 / 修复
#11517 — Web 聊天刷新会从屏幕和 localStorage 中丢失提示词 未列出修复 PR。
#12055 — MCP HTTP 客户端没有连接池/keep-alive 控制；陈旧 socket 会丢失工具调用 未列出修复 PR。
#12072 — Codex 流解码回退在非流式模式下重试并被拒绝 修复 PR #12073 已打开。
#12064 — Discord 明文审批可被白名单中的对等机器人应答 修复 PR #12065 已打开。

S3 — 次要

Issue 状态 / 修复
#12067 — untrusted_guard_sensitivity 使 prompt guard 和泄漏检测器朝相反方向变化 未列出修复 PR。
#12066 — Prompt guard 将任何分号或管道符标记为命令注入 修复 PR #12068 已打开。

已报告 / 活跃的安全问题

  • #12047 — OIDC bearer 验证没有尝试次数限制器或出站上限。
  • #12049 — 四个远程地址即可耗尽浏览器登录流程存储。
  • #12052 — 网关限流器以第一个 X-Forwarded-For 条目为键，从而可伪造回环豁免。
  • #12051 — sop_workshop apply 允许有范围限定的主体编写共享 SOP，而这些 SOP 之后会以操作员权限运行。
  • #12046 — 拥有通配符工具选择器的非管理员主体仍保留不感知主体的工具。
  • #11913 — Telegram 命令菜单全局暴露。

评估： 若干高严重度功能 bug 已有修复 PR，但大多数安全问题尚未有链接的修复 PR。同一报告者集中提交身份访问类发现，表明正在进行安全审计；这些问题应在 v0.9.0 之前优先处理。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

  • #11961 — 使用 OIDC 登录仪表板（标记为 release:v0.9.0）。是下一个次版本发布的有力候选，尤其是考虑到 #12047 中的相关安全工作。
  • #12069 — 面向 Code/ACP 会话的 /load-session。 已有 PR #12071；很可能在补丁版本或 v0.9.0 中落地。
  • #10705 — 为兼容的 OpenAI 模型支持 max 推理力度。 提供方对等性请求；一旦传输/配置处理确定，就可能发布。
  • #12077 — 为 fill-translations 提供页面上下文并增加第二读者评审。 面向文档本地化的流程/工具改进。
  • #7432 — v0.9.0 运行时/仪表板/网关跟踪器。 定义发布主题：运行时、登录和网关交付。

预测： v0.9.0 正围绕身份/访问（OIDC、主体范围限定）、运行时/网关交付、会话历史（#11921）以及知识图谱范围限定（#9745）成形。Android shell 和 Codex 流式传输修复更可能作为 v0.8.x 补丁落地。

7. 用户反馈摘要

过去 24 小时报告的痛点：

  • 由于 canonicalize 在 /system/bin/sh 上失败，Android/Termux 的 shell 工具调用实际上已不可用——对移动用户而言是硬性 S1 阻塞项。
  • 真实环境频繁变动下的 MCP 可靠性（容器重启、笔记本休眠、代理重载）较差；一次恢复失败就会污染会话，HTTP 连接池还可能静默丢失工具调用。
  • Web 仪表板在回合中途刷新时状态丢失会削弱对会话持久化的信任。
  • 安全态势担忧占主导：Telegram 命令暴露、OIDC 验证限制、代理头伪造、SOP 权限提升以及通配符工具选择器，都指向主体感知访问控制的缺口。
  • 本地化质量：多个文档 issue（#12076、#12078）指出 fr、ja、es 和 zh-CN 目录中存在英文残留和错误翻译。
  • 可用性摩擦：没有 /load-session 时恢复 Code 会话很繁琐；部分 OpenAI 兼容模型缺少推理力度控制。

满意信号： 快速发布节奏、由 19 位贡献者参与的安全导向 v0.8.7，以及针对 Android、Codex、Discord 和 prompt-guard 问题的快速修复 PR，体现了响应能力。

不满意信号： 高严重度阻塞项仍未关闭，许多安全发现缺少修复 PR，41 个 open PR 的积压可能延迟用户可见的修复。

8. 积压事项观察

条目 存在时长 / 状态 为何需要关注
#7432 — v0.9.0 运行时/仪表板/网关跟踪器 创建于 2026-06-09；16 条评论；今日更新 v0.9.0 核心跟踪器；需要排序和验收证据，以避免发布漂移。
#9745 — 知识图谱的按 agent 归因/范围限定 创建于 2026-08-04；needs-author-action；p1；v0.9.0；XL 与安全相关且受发布门控，但停滞于作者操作。
#10807 — MCP 连接污染 创建于 2026-09-12；p1；S1 修复 PR #12061 已存在但需要评审；用户影响大。
#10705 — 兼容 OpenAI 模型的 max 推理力度 创建于 2026-09-07；p2 提供方对等性请求，没有链接的 PR。
#11517 — Web 聊天刷新会丢失提示词 创建于 2026-10-04；p2；S2 无修复 PR；影响默认 session_persistence 行为。
#11414 — 聚焦工作区 创建于 2026-10-01；XL；risk:high 大型用户体验变更，需要维护者评审。
#11596 — 原生 Claude Code 账户 创建于 2026-10-07；needs-maintainer-review；risk:high 战略性接入功能；评审瓶颈。
#11680 — Firecrawl 网页搜索提供方 创建于 2026-10-12；needs-maintainer-review；XL 外部提供方集成，等待评审。
#11921 — 仅追加的会话事件历史 创建于 2026-10-21；XL；risk:high 基础架构变更；在 v0.9.0 之前需要仔细评审。

结论： ZeroClaw 在活跃度和发布纪律方面是健康的，但大量 open PR 队列、多个未解决的安全问题以及若干 S1/S2 bug 共同意味着，评审能力和安全分诊是下一个版本的关键路径。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。
