item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-28

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-28 01:35 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-28

1. Today's Overview

As of 2026-10-28, OpenClaw shows very high throughput: 500 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24h, with 391 active issues, 109 closed issues, 275 open PRs, and 225 merged/closed PRs. Three releases landed across beta, non-beta, and extended-stable channels, indicating active release engineering. However, the issue mix is heavily weighted toward production stability: at least nine open P0 issues appear in the top-50 sample, covering Gateway event-loop blocking, Windows/update failures, session/DB recovery, and memory bootstrap. Overall health is mixed: strong contributor/maintainer throughput and active community reproduction, but elevated stability risk because several high-comment P0/P1 issues still lack visible fix PRs.

2. Releases

Three new releases were published in the last 24h:

  • v2026.10.10-beta.4 — Beta release. Main stated fix: automations preserve authenticated operator authority for explicit same-conversation scheduled follow-ups, including one-shot next_check rearming, while retaining role, session, cancellation, target, and tool-policy revocation boundaries. No breaking changes or migration steps are stated in the supplied notes.
  • v2026.10.8 — Update-recovery focused release. Stated fixes include restarting the Gateway after an ordinary post-update Doctor failure instead of leaving it stopped; preventing an orphaned maintenance worker from blocking CLI commands and Gateway start; and avoiding update aborts on ACL filesystems and Windows-related update paths. No explicit breaking changes or migration notes are stated.
  • v2026.9.35 — Gateway-only extended-stable release, described as the current LTS equivalent. It is based on end-of-September 2026 OpenClaw plus critical security updates, reliability/performance fixes, and new model support.

Migration/breaking-change assessment: No breaking changes or explicit migration steps are listed in the supplied release text. v2026.10.8 is the most relevant release for operators recovering from failed post-update Gateway states; v2026.9.35 is the conservative extended-stable channel.

3. Project Progress

In the last 24h, 225 PRs were merged/closed and 275 remain open. The sample shows progress across security boundaries, update/restart reliability, session recovery, accessibility, and platform-specific fixes.

Closed/merged PR signals in the sample:

  • PR #186417 — Closed security fix: webhook, mapped-hook, plugin-trigger, and join-introduction turns no longer run with owner-only tools.
  • PR #183018 — Closed UI fix: keeps guest access guidance in Profile without misleading Inbox warnings.
  • PR #178347 — Closed docs fix: clarifies recovery for image-based hosts that stay down after an upgrade until Doctor runs.

Notable open/ready PRs advancing the project:

  • PR #185730 — Large refactor to resume running sessions after graceful restarts, reducing long restart drains and recovery contention.
  • PR #185939 — Recovers transcript rewrites from concurrent appends, targeting session/transcript integrity.
  • PR #186420 and PR #186426 — Improve model-fallback behavior on quota-class 429s instead of dead-ending on a pinned model or same-profile auth rotation.
  • PR #186415 — Prevents open node skill watches from deferring Gateway restarts for the full 300s.
  • PR #186411 — Fixes update cleanup failing its own destination check.
  • PR #185921 — Adds TUI screen reader mode, closing accessibility issue #9637 if merged.
  • PR #186416 — Restores iOS image shares on multi-agent gateways.
  • PR #185028 — Preserves native CORS preflights in browser navigation guards.
  • PR #184524 — Fixes quadratic re-scanning when streamed replies quote empty command output.
  • PR #184712 — Compacts consecutive Telegram progress tool calls to keep previews useful.

Closed issue signals in the sample: duplicate transcript writes (#118185), memory index stall after two files (#130955), billing cooldown recovery request (#115642), native Codex aborted-scope completion failure (#167410), memory index SIGTERM orphan issue (#185902), and update-failure reports (#169937, #153094).

4. Community Hot Topics

PR comment counts were blank in the supplied data, so hot-topic ranking below uses issue comment counts. Reaction counts are generally low; the most visible support in the sample is #7722 with 4 👍.

  • #160959 — 58 comments, P0. Gateway blocks for minutes while capturing large external/workspace plugins, a 2026.9.6 regression. Underlying need: plugin capture isolation, streaming limits, or async preparation so Gateway startup and runtime republishing cannot starve the event loop.
  • #119720 — 25 comments, P1. Synchronous agent persistence and transcript maintenance block the Gateway event loop at scale. Underlying need: async persistence, backpressure, and bounded transcript-maintenance work.
  • #170956 — 22 comments, P0. Windows managed-service installs show slow startup, unclean plugin shutdown, and schtasks permission errors, making restarts/updates unreliable. Underlying need: stronger Windows service lifecycle handling and update recovery.
  • #157325 — 19 comments, P0. A stuck agent-DB resource makes every agent’s replies fail until Gateway restart. Underlying need: DB resource health checks, automatic recovery, and per-agent failure isolation.
  • #120385 — 18 comments, P2. Code Mode tool catalog is incomplete for scheduled/cron and memory-flush turns, causing “Unknown tool id” failures. Underlying need: consistent tool discovery and catalog construction across all turn types.
  • Secondary high-engagement issues: #166634 (15 comments, P0 reclamation checkpoint failure), #121953 (14 comments, P1 DeepSeek cron prefix stall), #177656 (14 comments, P1 shared-state integrity error), and #172837 (14 comments, P1 Codex native subagent assignments not removed).

5. Bugs & Stability

P0 issues in the top-50 sample — highest severity:

  • #160959 — Gateway event loop blocks for minutes on large plugin capture. No new fix PR visible in provided tags.
  • #170956 — Windows slow startup, unclean plugin shutdown, and schtasks permission errors. No new fix PR visible.
  • #157325 — Stuck agent-DB resource causes all agent replies to fail until restart. Tagged needs-live-repro.
  • #166634 — Late reclamation checkpoint failure leaves agent unavailable after crash recovery. Tagged not-repro-on-main.
  • #161921 — state-migrated-no-rollback leaves doctor --fix and plugins update mutually blocked. No new fix PR visible.
  • #167406 — Windows MSIX Codex-enabled Gateway startup starves the main thread. No fix PR visible.
  • #185819 — Windows quick-start Codex onboarding completes device auth but fails activation with inactive harness runtime artifact. No fix PR visible.
  • #164800 — Managed update from 2026.9.7 to 2026.9.8 leaves activation driver dead until host reboot. No fix PR visible.
  • #158912 — MEMORY.md no longer injected at bootstrap on 2026.9.6 despite docs. No fix PR visible.

Selected P1 stability issues:

  • #119720 — Synchronous persistence/transcript maintenance blocks event loop.
  • #117262 — SQLite contention from three concurrent write handles causes ~33s event-loop stalls.
  • #121953 — Cron agent turns stall on DeepSeek because of the [cron:...] prefix.
  • #177656 — Native host exec returns shared-state integrity-admission error without child result.
  • #172837 — Codex native subagent assignments are never removed after completion delivery gives up.
  • #181432 — Excessive baseline RSS (~1.9 GB) and SQLite transaction timeouts in 2026.10.5.
  • #166017 — MCP session idle TTL default not applied; spawn broker reaches hard cap of 256 children. Has a linked open PR.
  • #169797 — Gateway memory regression and slower startup/first reply on single-CPU hosts.
  • #181078 — Agent turns intermittently fail with “Canonical session reader continuation is no longer current.”
  • #184720 — Windows interrupted update repair leaves empty Doctor custody receipts.
  • #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive idles 15+ minutes in plugin-capture stage.
  • #118776 — Leaf sub-agents keep sessions_yield but lose tools that could produce the awaited event.
  • #166964 — Subagent completion delivery fails permanently when requester authority is revoked.

Fix-PR visibility: The highest-comment P0s — #160959, #170956, #161921, #164800, and #185819 — do not show visible fix PRs in the supplied tags. Related open PRs exist for adjacent areas: transcript rewrite recovery (#185939), model fallback (#186420, #186426), restart deferral (#186415), update cleanup (#186411), browser CORS (#185028), and iOS image sharing (#186416).

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #7722 — Filesystem sandboxing config (tools.fileAccess) with allow/deny paths. Security-sensitive, 4 👍, tagged for product and security review. Important but unlikely to land without explicit security design.
  • #13219 — Per-model usage logging for cost tracking. Clear operator need; currently users must parse session JSONL manually.
  • #9637 — Accessibility option to disable emojis/unicode in TUI. An open implementation PR exists: #185921 adds screen reader mode, making this one of the more likely near-term UX improvements.
  • #52732 — Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list. Needs product decision; relevant for multi-agent deployments.
  • #175826 — Android parity for in-chat optional questions and native approval requests. Requests design acceptance before implementation.
  • #172547 — Exclude fenced dreaming ranges from memory-search indexing and recall signals. Needs product decision around memory semantics.
  • #184600 — Skill Workshop auto-mutation of skills without user review/consent. This is both a bug/UX concern and a governance/security roadmap signal.

Likely next-version candidates based on open PRs: TUI screen reader mode (#185921), model-fallback/quota handling (#186420, #186426), restart/update reliability (#186415, #186411), and session-resume/recovery work (#185730, #185939). Sandboxing, per-agent pruning, and Android approval parity look more dependent on product/security decisions.

7. User Feedback Summary

Dominant pain points: production reliability and upgrade safety. Users report Gateway event-loop stalls from plugin capture and persistence (#160959, #119720, #117262); Windows service/update failures (#170956, #164800, #184720, #185819); and update/doctor/plugin deadlocks (#161921).

Session and message integrity: repeated reports of stuck agent DB state (#157325), reclamation checkpoint failures (#166634), canonical session reader errors (#181078), duplicate transcript writes (#118185, closed), and subagent completion delivery failures (#166964).

Memory/indexing: missing MEMORY.md bootstrap (#158912), reindex lock preventing repair and accumulating 19 GB of temp DBs (#136311), full-index publish exhausting SQLite busy timeout (#143640), memory-bloat regressions (#181432, #169797), and dreaming ranker/applier mismatch (#121232).

Security/governance and UX: owner-only tools exposed to hook/join-introduction turns was fixed in #186417; users still ask for filesystem sandboxing (#7722) and governance of Skill Workshop auto-mutation (#184600). UX friction includes Control UI transcript jitter (#164394), webchat notice displacement (#177094), masked config values causing outage misdiagnosis (#173313), Telegram progress-preview crowding (#184712), and accessibility gaps (#9637, #185921).

Sentiment assessment: no survey data is provided, but issue sentiment is strained around production stability and upgrades. Positive signals are active community reproduction, detailed operator reports, linked PRs, and maintainer triage labels; dissatisfaction is concentrated in repeated P0/P1 reliability failures and insufficient rollback/diagnostic paths.

8. Backlog Watch

These items are old or high-impact, have significant discussion, and still need maintainer attention:

  • #160959 — P0 since 2026-09-29, 58 comments, no new fix PR. Highest-priority Gateway event-loop blocker.
  • #119720 — P1 since 2026-08-05, 25 comments, no new fix PR. Long-running persistence/event-loop scaling issue.
  • #117262 — P1 since 2026-08-01, 12 comments. SQLite write-handle contention causing ~33s stalls.
  • #121953 — P1 since 2026-08-11, 14 comments. DeepSeek cron-prefix stall remains unresolved.
  • #136311 — P2 since 2026-09-02, 12 comments. Memory reindex lock and orphaned temp DB accumulation.
  • #161921 — P0 since 2026-09-30, 11 comments, no new fix PR. Update/doctor/plugin deadlock blocks recovery.
  • #170956 — P0 since 2026-10-13, 22 comments, no new fix PR. Windows restart/update reliability.
  • #7722 — P2 security enhancement since 2026-02-03, 11 comments, 4 👍. Filesystem sandboxing config needs product/security decision.
  • #13219 — P2 since 2026-02-10, 9 comments. Per-model usage logging for cost tracking.
  • #52732 — P2 since 2026-03-23, 7 comments. Per-agent compaction/context-pruning overrides need product decision.

PR backlog note: Most high-impact PRs in the sample are recent. The clearest older PR is #156626, a test-only relay-matching refactor open since 2026-09-23 and waiting on author; it is low product risk relative to the P0/P1 issue backlog.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

1. Ecosystem Overview

On 2026-10-28, the personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape is consolidating around a gateway/runtime core, multi-surface clients (desktop, web, mobile, messaging), and MCP/tool integrations. Activity is high but uneven: OpenClaw operates at hyper-scale, Hermes Agent, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw iterate in the 22–50 issue/PR range, and IronClaw was inactive in the window. Release engineering is becoming a differentiator—OpenClaw shipped three channels, QwenPaw a beta, ZeroClaw a security patch, while Hermes shipped no release. The common drag is no longer feature breadth but production hardening: session identity, async runtime health, provider compatibility, MCP reliability, and principal-aware security.

2. Activity Comparison

Counts are 24h updated/touched, not repository totals. Health score* is an analyst heuristic combining activity, release cadence, stability/security, and review throughput; it is not an upstream project metric.

Project Issues count (24h) PR count (24h) Release status Health score*
OpenClaw 500 updated: 391 open/active, 109 closed 500 updated: 275 open, 225 merged/closed 3 releases: beta, update-recovery stable, extended-stable LTS 6.5/10 — high throughput, elevated P0 risk
Hermes Agent 50 touched: 47 open, 3 closed 50 touched: 43 open, 7 merged/closed No release; users reference v0.22.5 stable 5.8/10 — high triage, session-architecture debt
IronClaw No activity No activity No release N/A — inactive window
QwenPaw 36 touched: 16 open, 20 closed 50 touched: 39 open, 11 merged/closed v2.3.0-beta.1 7.0/10 — responsive, review backlog
ZeroClaw 22 updated: 21 open, 1 closed 42 updated: 41 open, 1 merged/closed v0.8.7 security/maintenance 6.7/10 — release discipline, security/review bottleneck

3. OpenClaw’s Position

Advantages vs peers. OpenClaw is the scale leader by an order of magnitude: 500 issues and 500 PRs touched in 24h, with 225 PRs merged/closed—versus 7 for Hermes, 11 for QwenPaw, and 1 for ZeroClaw. It is also the only project in this set with three active release channels, including an extended-stable LTS-equivalent. Its issue engagement is the deepest in the sample: the top Gateway event-loop issue has 58 comments, versus 24 for Hermes’ top item, 16 for ZeroClaw, and 5 for QwenPaw.

Technical approach differences. OpenClaw is a horizontal, Gateway-centric platform: sessions, plugins, channels, Doctor/update recovery, and security boundaries are centralized in a runtime that is visibly sensitive to event-loop blocking. Peers are narrower and more vertical: Hermes is building a canonical multi-surface session/protocol layer; QwenPaw is concentrated on desktop/console context, memory, MCP, and provider compatibility; ZeroClaw is security-first with OIDC, principal scoping, and a Rust/Tokio/Wasmtime-style stack. OpenClaw’s advantage is breadth and operator tooling; its risk is that the same central runtime concentrates production stability failures.

Community size comparison. OpenClaw’s throughput is not just larger—it is a different operating tier. It closed/merged 225 PRs in 24h, roughly 20–30x the visible merge throughput of Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw. That implies a much larger contributor/maintainer base and more production deployment surface, but also a harder triage problem: at least nine open P0s appear in the top-50 sample, and several top P0s lack visible fix PRs.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Shared need Projects showing it Specific requirements
Session persistence, resumption, and identity OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw Resumable sessions across restarts and surfaces; explicit ownership instead of source-based locking; recovery from transcript/DB corruption; append-only event history; session load/resume APIs.
Async runtime health and backpressure OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw Non-blocking persistence and plugin capture; bounded queues; SQLite contention control; gateway stall detection; per-profile thread/resource limits; MCP connection recovery.
Provider/model compatibility and cost-aware fallback OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw Quota-aware 429 fallback; wire-format quirks such as thinking-disable shapes; OAuth/subscription sign-in; Codex streaming behavior; model catalog drift; typed provider errors.
MCP/tool protocol and tool-call integrity OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw Legacy MCP negotiation fallback; poisoned-session recovery; consistent tool catalog per turn; schema/argument validation; approval-path safety; principal-aware tool selectors.
Security, governance, and least privilege OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw Filesystem sandboxing; audit-log integrity; OIDC/SSO; CSP; owner-only tool boundaries; approval allowlist hardening; protection against subagent/plugin privilege escalation.
Upgrade/install reliability and multi-surface parity OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw Self-healing updates and rollback; Windows/Android install robustness; diagnostics that preserve failure causes; mobile keyboard/input; PWA/Linux packaging; accessibility modes.

IronClaw has no data in this window and is excluded from the shared-need evidence.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Project Primary feature focus Target users Architecture / approach
OpenClaw Broad gateway/plugin platform, multi-channel operations, update recovery, LTS Operators, power users, production multi-channel deployments Gateway-centric core; plugins/channels; Doctor/update paths; extended-stable release channel; event-loop-sensitive runtime.
Hermes Agent Multi-surface conversation continuity and client protocol Power users, remote hermes serve deployments, third-party client builders Canonical session authority + gateway; Desktop/Webapp/mobile/TUI surfaces; profile multiplexing; currently paying down session-ownership debt.
QwenPaw Desktop/console agent workspace, context compaction, memory, MCP/provider breadth, governance Desktop and enterprise users needing MCP, memory, audit, and provider flexibility Python-based console/desktop stack; skills/channels/plugins; SQLite history; model registry; governance audit; Windows/Linux packaging.
ZeroClaw Security-first self-hosted gateway/dashboard, identity/access, runtime hardening Security-conscious self-hosters and enterprise-style deployments Rust/Tokio/Wasmtime stack; gateway/dashboard; OIDC and principal scoping; append-only session history; v0.9.0 runtime/gateway focus.
IronClaw No visible activity in window Unknown Unknown from supplied data.

OpenClaw is the horizontal platform play. Hermes is the multi-surface continuity play. QwenPaw is the desktop/context/provider-compatibility play. ZeroClaw is the security/identity play. That differentiation is healthy, but all four are converging on the same operational requirements: restart-safe sessions, async runtime isolation, provider abstraction, MCP robustness, and least-privilege tool access.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Tier 1 — hyper-scale, release-engineered: OpenClaw. Highest activity by far, 225 merged/closed PRs in 24h, three releases including an LTS-equivalent. It is rapidly iterating, but maturity is uneven: strong release engineering and community reproduction coexist with multiple P0 stability issues and missing visible fix PRs on top blockers.

Tier 2 — high-velocity stabilizers: QwenPaw, ZeroClaw, and Hermes Agent.

  • QwenPaw is the most responsive fixer in the sample: 20 issues closed, 11 PRs merged/closed, and several same-day/near-day issue→PR pairs. Its constraint is review bandwidth, with 39 open PRs and several multi-week size/XXXL efforts.
  • ZeroClaw has strong release discipline—v0.8.7 with 81 commits from 19 contributors—and a clear v0.9.0 security/identity theme. The bottleneck is review/security triage: 41 open PRs vs 1 merged/closed, and several security findings have no fix PR yet.
  • Hermes Agent is triage-heavy rather than merge-heavy: 47 open issues, 43 open PRs, 7 merged/closed, no release. The Webapp post-merge aftershock and session-ownership cluster suggest it is stabilizing under architectural debt rather than shipping net-new surface area.

Tier 3 — inactive window: IronClaw had no activity in the last 24h; no momentum or maturity judgment is possible from this digest.

7. Trend Signals

Industry trend Evidence from community feedback Value for AI agent developers
Session continuity is becoming the product Hermes’ top issues are “listed but unopenable” sessions across Desktop/mobile/Webapp/TUI; OpenClaw has restart/session/DB recovery work; ZeroClaw loses prompts on reload; QwenPaw sessions break after provider switches. Design session identity, ownership, and a resumable event log early. Treat “one conversation across surfaces and restarts” as a core contract, not a UI feature.
Reliability is now a feature, not an ops afterthought OpenClaw event-loop blocking, SQLite stalls, update/Doctor deadlocks; Hermes gateway stalls under load; QwenPaw compaction aborts; ZeroClaw poisoned MCP sessions. Build async persistence, bounded queues, health checks, rollback paths, and diagnostic preservation into the runtime from day one.
Provider abstraction must be capability-based, not model-name-based OpenClaw quota-aware fallback; QwenPaw thinking-disable/wire-format quirks; ZeroClaw Codex streaming and reasoning effort; Hermes ChatGPT sign-in provider. Implement typed provider capabilities, quota-aware fallback, OAuth/subscription auth, and per-provider error normalization.
MCP/tool interoperability is the integration battleground QwenPaw legacy MCP negotiation failures; ZeroClaw poisoned MCP sessions and stale sockets; OpenClaw tool catalog gaps and MCP spawn caps; Hermes tool-argument schema failures. Invest in MCP negotiation fallback, session recovery, schema validation, and consistent tool discovery across turn types.
Security is shifting left into the agent runtime ZeroClaw’s OIDC/XFF/SOP/principal-scoping findings; OpenClaw sandboxing and owner-tool fixes; Hermes approval allowlist bypass; QwenPaw audit-log integrity and out-of-workspace writes. Adopt principal-aware tool access, audit trails, sandboxing, CSP, and secure defaults for plugins, hooks, subagents, and messaging surfaces.
Multi-surface parity and accessibility are becoming baseline expectations Hermes mobile keyboard/viewport issues; OpenClaw TUI screen-reader mode and iOS sharing; QwenPaw Windows/Linux packaging; ZeroClaw Android shell failure. Share one protocol across clients, but budget for mobile input, viewport, accessibility, packaging, and platform-specific lifecycle behavior.
Maintainer review bandwidth is the scaling constraint QwenPaw’s 39 open PRs and multi-week XXXL work; ZeroClaw’s 41 open PRs; Hermes’ 43:7 open-to-merged ratio; OpenClaw’s P0s without visible fix PRs. Modular ownership, design-doc gates for large changes, and triage automation matter as much as contributor growth once a project reaches mid-scale.

Bottom line: the ecosystem is moving from “agent demos” to “agent infrastructure.” The winners will be projects that make sessions portable, runtimes non-blocking, providers interchangeable, MCP recoverable, and permissions auditable—without losing multi-surface usability or release velocity.

7. User Feedback Summary

Satisfaction drivers visible in the data: users are running genuinely demanding workloads — multi-profile gateways (3 and 28 profile installs appear), load-30–100 macOS hosts, 200+ gateway threads, cron chains, Kanban worker fleets, remote hermes serve behind basic auth, and third-party mobile clients built on the protocol (Hy4ri's Android client, an iOS "Cadu" client). The fact that people are building clients against Hermes is a strong ecosystem signal.

Dissatisfaction / pain points, in order of volume:

  1. "My conversation vanished." The dominant complaint. Sessions are listed but unopenable, and several reports note the failure is silent (TUI starts a fresh session; Desktop send is cancelled with no toast). Users perceive this as data loss even when rows exist.
  2. Opaque failure messages. #143874 ("every ticket failure reads the same string"), #145286 (policy refusal rendered as a model-connection error), and #143561 all describe the same frustration: the system knows why it failed and throws that away one line earlier.
  3. Operational fragility on Windows and loaded hosts. Stale gateway.pid breaking hermes update every run, plus gateway timeouts under load, were both closed today — but they are exactly the kind of issues that drive users off the stable channel.
  4. Mobile is second-class. Android soft keyboard drops input, long messages eat 90% of the viewport, per-tab menus are unreachable on touch. Three separate issues, one theme.
  5. First-run / setup confusion. "Needs setup" pills on platforms that are already enabled undermines trust in the settings surface.

Engagement caveat: reaction counts are very low across the board (maximum 👍 is 2 on a 24-comment issue). Discussion volume is carried by a small number of deeply-invested power users rather than broad community voting — worth weighing when prioritizing by 👍.

  • #8034 size/L — bound inline media per request, not per file; directly relevant to the #8290/#8171 media-wedge family, open since 2026-09-29.
  • #8178 size/XL, first-time contributor — nested skill directories, open since 2026-10-11.
  • #8210 size/S, first-time contributor — Windows Creator project delete (WinError 5), open since 2026-10-13; small and low-risk.

Recommendation: the ratio of 39 open PRs to 11 closed in 24h, combined with four multi-week XXXL PRs, indicates review bandwidth — not contributor supply — is the current constraint. Triage of size/S–size/M first-time-contributor PRs (#8210, #8454, #8178) and a consolidated fix for the MCP-negotiation and media-classifier families would yield the highest health-per-hour.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-28

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw remains highly active: 22 issues and 42 PRs were updated in the last 24 hours, alongside the v0.8.7 security release. The project closed only one issue (#9101) and one PR (#12019), while 21 issues and 41 PRs remain open, indicating that contribution volume is outpacing merge/review throughput. Activity is concentrated in security and identity-access hardening, v0.9.0 runtime/gateway work, and reliability fixes for MCP, Android, Discord, and OpenAI Codex. Overall project health is strong on community engagement and release cadence, but the growing open-PR backlog is the main operational constraint.

Data caveat: PR comment counts were provided as undefined, so PR discussion activity cannot be ranked reliably. The v0.8.7 changelog excerpt is truncated.

2. Releases

v0.8.7 — Security and maintenance follow-up to v0.8.6

  • Scope: 81 commits from 19 contributors.
  • Key changes:
    • Moves to patched Wasmtime and Rustls certificate verification.
    • Updates tokio and ctutils for advisories affecting v0.8.6.
    • Rebuilds container images.
  • Breaking changes / migration: None explicitly listed in the provided notes. This appears to be a patch-level security release; operators should upgrade promptly given the advisory fixes.
  • Follow-up work already tracked: Translation/catalogue fixes in #12076 and the translation pin in #12079.

3. Project Progress

Merged / closed today

  • [PR #12019] chore(docs): pin translations to v0.8.7 — link. The sole merged/closed PR in the last 24h; moves the docs catalogue gitlink to the v0.8.7 translations tag.
  • [Issue #9101] Consolidate release attestation mechanisms — link. Closed after 11 comments; addresses redundant cosign, GitHub attestation, and SLSA signing paths that inflated release assets to ~53.

Fixes advanced via open PRs

  • Android shell failure: #12080 adds a fallback when canonicalize("/system/bin/sh") hits EPERM, addressing #12075.
  • OpenAI Codex streaming: #12073 retries Codex streams as streams instead of stream: false, addressing #12072.
  • Prompt guard false positives: #12068 stops treating bare ; or | as command injection, addressing #12066.
  • Discord approvals: #12065 prevents allowlisted peer bots from answering plaintext approvals, addressing #12064.
  • MCP recovery: #12061 attempts to recover poisoned MCP sessions, addressing #10807.
  • ZeroCode session resume: #12071 adds /load-session, addressing #12069.
  • Runtime prompt ordering: #12056 keeps identity sections at the head of direct-path system prompts.
  • Channel prompt cap: #12070 re-applies the system prompt cap after per-turn skill refreshes.

Larger features in flight

  • #11921 — append-only session event history (XL, risk:high).
  • #11414 — opt-in focused workspaces for the web dashboard (XL, risk:high).
  • #11880 — transport-neutral Goal policy contracts.
  • #11596 — native Claude Code account onboarding.
  • #11680 — Firecrawl web search provider.
  • #12059 — runtime-profile thinking levels for OpenAI.

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Comments Why it matters
#7432 — Runtime, dashboard sign-in and gateway delivery tracker 16 Long-running v0.9.0 tracker. Signals demand for coordinated release allocation and acceptance evidence across runtime/gateway work.
#9101 — Consolidate release attestation mechanisms 11 Closed today. Reflects maintainer/contributor concern over CI cost and release complexity from three parallel signing mechanisms.
#11517 — Web chat reload drops prompt 3 Session persistence is still unreliable under mid-turn reloads; directly affects dashboard usability.
#10807 — MCP connection permanently poisoned 3 A single failed recovery attempt blocks workflows; high-impact for MCP-heavy users.
#11913 — Telegram command menu exposed to all users 2 Security/privacy concern: setMyCommands lacks trusted-user scoping.
#11961 — Dashboard sign-in with OIDC 2 Identity/access demand for enterprise-style SSO on the web dashboard.
#12047 — OIDC bearer verification lacks limiter 2 Security hardening gap around outbound token checks.

Underlying needs: The hottest discussions cluster around (1) release engineering simplification (#9101), (2) coordinated v0.9.0 runtime/gateway planning (#7432), and (3) security/identity-access correctness (#11913, #11961, #12047). PR comment counts were not available, but large/risky PRs such as #11921 and #9745 are likely review bottlenecks.

5. Bugs & Stability

S1 — Workflow blocked

Issue Status / Fix
#10807 — MCP connection permanently poisoned by one failed recovery attempt (p1, risk:high) Fix PR #12061 open.
#12075 — Android shell tool always fails; /system/bin/sh canonicalization EPERM Fix PR #12080 open.

S2 — Degraded behavior

Issue Status / Fix
#11517 — Web chat reload drops prompt from screen and localStorage No fix PR listed.
#12055 — MCP HTTP client has no pool/keep-alive control; stale socket loses tool call No fix PR listed.
#12072 — Codex stream-decode fallback retries without streaming and is rejected Fix PR #12073 open.
#12064 — Discord plaintext approvals can be answered by an allowlisted peer bot Fix PR #12065 open.

S3 — Minor

Issue Status / Fix
#12067 — untrusted_guard_sensitivity moves prompt guard and leak detector in opposite directions No fix PR listed.
#12066 — Prompt guard flags any semicolon or pipe as command injection Fix PR #12068 open.

Security issues reported / active

  • #12047 — OIDC bearer verification has no attempt limiter or outbound cap.
  • #12049 — Four remote addresses can exhaust the browser sign-in flow store.
  • #12052 — Gateway limiters key on the first X-Forwarded-For entry, enabling loopback-exemption spoofing.
  • #12051 — sop_workshop apply lets a scoped principal author shared SOPs that later run with operator authority.
  • #12046 — Non-admin principals with wildcard tool selectors retain principal-unaware tools.
  • #11913 — Telegram command menu exposed globally.

Assessment: Fix PRs exist for several high-severity functional bugs, but most security issues have no linked fix PR yet. The concentration of identity-access findings from the same reporter suggests an ongoing security audit; these should be prioritized before v0.9.0.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • #11961 — Dashboard sign-in with OIDC (tagged release:v0.9.0). Strong candidate for the next minor release, especially given related security work in #12047.
  • #12069 — /load-session for Code/ACP sessions. Already has PR #12071; likely to land in a patch or v0.9.0.
  • #10705 — Support max reasoning effort for compatible OpenAI models. Provider parity request; could ship once transport/config handling is settled.
  • #12077 — Give fill-translations page context and add second-reader review. Process/tooling improvement for docs localization.
  • #7432 — v0.9.0 runtime/dashboard/gateway tracker. Defines the release theme: runtime, sign-in, and gateway delivery.

Prediction: v0.9.0 is shaping up around identity/access (OIDC, principal scoping), runtime/gateway delivery, session history (#11921), and knowledge-graph scoping (#9745). Android shell and Codex streaming fixes are more likely to land as v0.8.x patches.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points reported in the last 24h:

  • Android/Termux is effectively broken for shell tool calls due to canonicalize failing on /system/bin/sh — a hard S1 blocker for mobile users.
  • MCP reliability under real-world churn (container restarts, laptop sleep, proxy reloads) is poor; one failed recovery poisons the session, and HTTP pooling can silently lose tool calls.
  • Web dashboard state loss on reload mid-turn erodes trust in session persistence.
  • Security posture concerns dominate: Telegram command exposure, OIDC verification limits, proxy-header spoofing, SOP privilege escalation, and wildcard tool selectors all point to gaps in principal-aware access control.
  • Localization quality: multiple docs issues (#12076, #12078) cite English leftovers and incorrect translations in fr, ja, es, and zh-CN catalogues.
  • Usability friction: resuming Code sessions is cumbersome without /load-session; reasoning effort control is missing for some OpenAI-compatible models.

Satisfaction signals: Rapid release cadence, a security-focused v0.8.7 with 19 contributors, and quick fix PRs for Android, Codex, Discord, and prompt-guard issues show responsiveness.

Dissatisfaction signals: High-severity blockers remain open, many security findings lack fix PRs, and the 41-open-PR backlog may delay user-visible fixes.

8. Backlog Watch

Item Age / Status Why it needs attention
#7432 — v0.9.0 runtime/dashboard/gateway tracker Created 2026-06-09; 16 comments; updated today Central v0.9.0 tracker; needs sequencing and acceptance evidence to avoid release drift.
#9745 — Per-agent attribution/scoping for knowledge graph Created 2026-08-04; needs-author-action; p1; v0.9.0; XL Security-relevant and release-gated, but stalled on author action.
#10807 — MCP connection poisoning Created 2026-09-12; p1; S1 Fix PR #12061 exists but needs review; high user impact.
#10705 — max reasoning effort for compatible OpenAI models Created 2026-09-07; p2 Provider parity request with no linked PR.
#11517 — Web chat reload drops prompt Created 2026-10-04; p2; S2 No fix PR; affects default session_persistence behavior.
#11414 — Focused workspaces Created 2026-10-01; XL; risk:high Large UX change needing maintainer review.
#11596 — Native Claude Code accounts Created 2026-10-07; needs-maintainer-review; risk:high Strategic onboarding feature; review bottleneck.
#11680 — Firecrawl web search provider Created 2026-10-12; needs-maintainer-review; XL External provider integration awaiting review.
#11921 — Append-only session event history Created 2026-10-21; XL; risk:high Foundational architecture change; needs careful review before v0.9.0.

Bottom line: ZeroClaw is healthy on activity and release discipline, but the combination of a large open-PR queue, multiple unaddressed security issues, and several S1/S2 bugs means review capacity and security triage are the critical path for the next release.

item.content:encoded:
AI 基础设施日报 2026-10-28

生成时间: 2026-10-28 01:35 UTC | 覆盖项目: 6 个

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

横向对比

跨项目 AI 基础设施对比 — 2026-10-28

范围：vLLM、SGLang、llama.cpp、Ollama、LiteLLM、Unsloth。
n/r = 提供的 24 小时摘要中未报告。SGLang 是唯一提供明确 24 小时 issue/PR 数的项目。

1. 生态概览

生态系统目前处于硬件认证与正确性加固阶段，而非大版本发布阶段。推理服务引擎正在竞相覆盖 DeepSeek-V4、Qwen3.8、Kimi-K3、GLM-5.x，以及 SM120、ROCm MI355X 和 GB300 等新加速器目标，但若干高严重度问题属于静默正确性缺陷或进程终止类 bug，而非吞吐量回退。本地运行时正在快速吸收新的 LiquidAI LFM3 系列，尤其是 llama.cpp；Ollama 随后跟进修复和 MLX 并发工作。网关层仍在发布补丁，但仍存在安全补丁回溯缺口和计费正确性问题。微调工具聚焦于 Studio 加固和 FP8/Block Swap 修复，新模型支持落后于服务引擎。

2. 活跃度对比

Project Issues count (24h) PR count (24h) Release status Activity signal
vLLM n/r n/r 无发布；无破坏性变更 硬件/模型覆盖增加，同时存在严重回归。#50576 有 121 条评论；#56892 是严重的 SM120 CUDA-graph/decode 问题。
SGLang 63 个已更新 500 个已更新 无发布 路线图/跟踪器整合，以及大规模 [inactive] 陈旧项清理。#43412 是严重的 spec-decode 崩溃，#45755 是 Kimi-K3 SM90 静默 bug。
llama.cpp n/r n/r 持续构建 b11930–b11944；无正式发布 LFM3 系列已在文本/视觉/音频/omni 上落地；reasoning-effort 发现和 router 内存上限已交付。
Ollama n/r n/r 无发布 LFM3 GGUF 修复、MLX 并发生成、CUDA/Blackwell 启动缓解。多个 macOS/MLX 和工具循环问题尚未解决。
LiteLLM n/r n/r 4 个补丁发布：v1.106.5、v1.105.6、v1.104.8、v1.103.10；main 为 1.109.0；1.108.0 为 RC 1.106.x 镜像的安全补丁回溯仍未完成；多项流式/计费和 slot 泄漏修复。
Unsloth n/r n/r 无发布 Studio 加固；Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 的 FP8/Block Swap 修复；Windows 回收站和 Anthropic 自动压缩回归。

3. 模型支持竞赛

Project New model / architecture support today Assessment
vLLM SM8x 上的 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 仍是开放请求，尚未支持；Kimi NVFP4 PR；Nemotron-Nano 工具解析器；AMD CDNA W4A16；ROCm Inv-RoPE FP8；Qwen2.5-Omni CPU offload 数据中心覆盖广泛，但 Ampere 用户仍无法运行 DeepSeek-V4-Flash。SM120 上的 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 是严重风险。
SGLang Nemotron-3-Embed 原生支持；DeepSeek-V4 的混合 NVFP4/MXFP4 draft experts；NPU DSpark 紧凑模式；AMD RDNA3/RDNA4 跟踪；Apple Silicon RFC 在数据中心/PD 和加速器特定路径上较强，但 Kimi-K3 SM90 MXFP4 存在 静默激活函数替换 bug。
llama.cpp LFM3-1.7B、LFM3-VL-2B、LFM3-Audio-2B、LFM3-Omni-2B；LiquidAI d1-2B/d1-omni-2B；LFM3 的视频输入；/v1/realtime 工具调用；GigaChat 3.5 432B-A28B 已提议 目前 LFM3 支持最领先，包括多模态、音频/omni 和实时工具链路。
Ollama 在 unknown model architecture: 'lfm3' 后修复 LFM3 GGUF；Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B；Kolibri 1 MLX；MLX 并发生成；CUDA/Blackwell 启动修复 在 LFM3 上跟随 llama.cpp；本地运行时打包能力强，但 MLX 和 CUDA 启动回归仍然存在。
LiteLLM 不是推理运行时。Databricks OpenJev 定价修复；Cloudflare Workers AI 扩展仍停滞；Tavily 透传 模型支持意味着 provider/pricing/API 覆盖，而非架构启用。
Unsloth 仅有 LFM3 请求，无实现 PR；Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8/Block Swap 修复；Intel Arc XPU 请求；AMD 混合 Linux 检测问题；ExLlamaV3 请求 微调支持 落后于新模型启用；Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 是修补最活跃的架构。

领先者：

  • 数据中心服务： vLLM 和 SGLang 在 DeepSeek-V4、Qwen3.8、Kimi-K3、GLM-5.x、ROCm MI355X 和 SM120/GB300 路径上领先。vLLM 的硬件/模型覆盖更广；SGLang 在 PD 分离、缓存感知路由和加速器特定内核上更激进。
  • 本地/边缘运行时： llama.cpp 在 LFM3 和本地多模态/实时方面领先；Ollama 位居第二，但仍在修复 LFM3 GGUF/MLX 问题。
  • 微调： Unsloth 在加速方面较强，但尚未交付 LFM3 支持；Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 修复是主要的新架构工作。

4. 性能前沿

Optimization area Where effort is concentrated Representative items
KV 缓存、前缀缓存与卸载 内存压力、PD 陈旧 KV 正确性、前缀共享与缓存卸载可扩展性 vLLM P2P KV 卸载快速失败、投机解码下的 KV-pool 崩溃、multi-tier/GDS RFC；SGLang HiCache ack 队列排空、MLA+FP8 KV 物化占 decode step 的 43.7%；llama.cpp --slot-attach 前缀共享；Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 上的 Unsloth Block Swap 卸载。
内核与量化 FP8/FP4/W4A16 内核、MoE 专家路径、small-M GEMM 和后端特定内核 vLLM SSM GDN 原地状态（+10–13% 吞吐，每步流量最多减少 36 GiB）、CDNA W4A16、ROCm Inv-RoPE FP8、MI355X 跟踪项；SGLang 面向 GLM-5.2 block-FP8 的 W8A16 small-M GEMM（每 token 延迟最多降低 6.8%）、DeepGEMM fp8_fp4、GDN Triton 修复；llama.cpp MoE 专家缓存（+6% QFN，+7% GLM）、Hexagon TOP_K、CUDA-graph cluster-dim 重新实例化。
批处理、调度与分布式服务 PD 分离、DP/EP 协调、弹性 EP、缓存感知路由 vLLM 在 MoE+DP 下的 NCCL reduce_scatter 死锁、弹性 EP 中重复 CUDA-graph 捕获、CPU offload 的 PP-rank 不一致；SGLang PD 分离路线图、sm_120 上 EP2 非法内存访问、agentic 缓存调度；llama.cpp router --models-memory-max 与 RPC 加固；LiteLLM 路由/slot 泄漏。
低延迟 API 与流式传输 Guardrail 流式传输、embedding 超时、计时头、reasoning-effort 发现 LiteLLM 为仅请求型 guardrail 恢复流式快速路径，并修复 embedding 超时传播；vLLM 提议可选启用的 x-vllm-* 计时头；llama.cpp 暴露 reasoning-effort 级别；SGLang 收紧 OpenAI 兼容校验。
本地/边缘与微调内存 MLX 并发、CUDA 启动、Windows 桌面磁盘占用、显式量化选择 Ollama 通过 OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL 实现 MLX 并行、CUDA eager-module 启动重试；Unsloth Block Swap/FP8 n-gram 修复、基准测试页面工作、Windows 回收站 WAL/SHM 泄漏。

重心很清楚：KV-cache/内存行为、FP8/FP4/MoE 内核以及 PD/分布式调度主导工程投入。原始吞吐量工作越来越与正确性验证耦合，尤其是在投机解码和量化目标周围。

5. 层级定位

Layer Projects Role Today’s signal
高吞吐服务引擎 vLLM、SGLang 数据中心 GPU/加速器推理、OpenAI 兼容 API、分布式服务、PD 分离、高级量化 两者都处于硬件/模型覆盖竞赛中；性能收益是真实的，但关键正确性和稳定性问题仍然存在。vLLM 更广；SGLang 在 PD/缓存/内核上更激进。
本地/边缘运行时与服务器 llama.cpp、Ollama 单节点/本地推理、广泛量化、CPU/GPU/后端覆盖、多模态/音频、面向开发者的模型管理 llama.cpp 交付新架构最快；Ollama 在做打包和加固，尤其是 MLX/CUDA/LFM3。两者都不能替代集群级服务引擎。
LLM 网关/代理 LiteLLM 路由、预算、支出日志、认证、provider 转换、guardrail、OpenAI/Anthropic 兼容代理 发布节奏快，但安全补丁回溯和计费正确性问题意味着必须固定版本并核对支出。
微调/训练加速 Unsloth 微调、量化训练/导出、桌面 Studio、基准测试 聚焦 Studio 加固和 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8/Block Swap 修复；新模型支持和硬件覆盖落后于服务运行时。

6. 趋势信号

  • 硬件-量化认证现已成为首要生产任务。 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 在 SM8x 上仍然缺失，SM120 CUDA graph 对 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 已损坏，sm_120 + EP2 对某些 NVFP4 checkpoint 不可用，Intel XPU / 混合 NVIDIA-AMD / 消费级 Radeon 仍是空白。应将硬件 + 模型 + 量化视为经过测试的元组，而不是笼统的“CUDA”或“ROCm”目标。
  • 在风险层面，正确性 bug 正在超过性能收益。 SGLang 的 Kimi-K3 SM90 MXFP4 静默计算错误的激活，llama.cpp 投机解码在量化目标上发生偏离，vLLM 贪心输出可能在重启之间变化，SGLang PD prefill 存在陈旧 KV 风险。输出一致性和前缀共享回归测试应作为升级门槛。
  • 投机解码和 MoE 仍是高杠杆但高风险。 vLLM、SGLang、llama.cpp、Ollama 和 Unsloth 目前都在涉及 draft 模型、MTP、专家缓存或 spec-decode 路径。模式一致：潜在收益很大，但在量化/MoE/PD 配置周围会出现崩溃、挂起、静默偏离或精度骤降。
  • PD 分离和缓存感知路由正成为 agent 的默认架构方向。 SGLang 的 PD 和 agentic-cache 路线图、vLLM 的 KV offload RFC，以及 llama.cpp 的前缀共享，都指向同一个问题：长前缀、多轮 agent 循环成本高昂，因此 KV 局部性和缓存路由成为控制面关注点。
  • Agent/工具兼容性正在碎片化。 vLLM 的 Rust 前端在 auto 工具解析器上可能返回 500；Ollama 存在工具循环 500 和静默丢弃工具调用；LiteLLM 的 /v1/messages 路径是变动最频繁的表面；llama.cpp 正在添加 tool_reference 和实时工具调用。应用开发者应针对固定版本验证工具调用顺序、空内容处理、未知工具行为和参数边界。
  • 供应链和 DoS 加固重新提上日程。 LiteLLM 1.106.x 镜像仍信任一个已泄露的根 CA，llama.cpp 有一个待处理的 RPC ggml_nbytes() 溢出修复，未设边界的 sampler 参数可触发数 GB 分配。网关和服务器部署需要 cosign 验证、输入上限和不可信对端假设。
  • 本地多模态和语音 agent 正变得实用。 llama.cpp 中的 LFM3 文本/视觉/音频/omni 支持、Ollama 的 MLX 工作，以及实时转写/工具调用端点，都指向跨越文本、音频和视频的本地 agent。在扩展多会话本地部署之前，关注 co-batching 和混合状态正确性问题。

按严重程度排序：

严重

  • SM120 CUDA graph 不可用 + 解码吞吐极低：DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 在 8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 上使用 --enforce-eager 时出现。该 issue 中尚未确定修复方案。#56892

中

  • 投机解码时 KV cache 池崩溃：当 draft 模型引入新的 cache spec 类型（hybrid GDN + DFlash）时发生；已有专用 draft 池的 POC。#59117

进行中的修复 PR

6. 这对应用开发者意味着什么

  • A100/A800 用户目前仍无法运行 DeepSeek-V4-Flash——请规划 Hopper/Blackwell 容量，或等待 #50576 中跟踪的 SM8x 支持。

4. 性能与优化

已合入 / 提议的内核

  • #45862 — 面向 GLM-5.2 block-FP8 解码投影的 W8A16 small-M GEMM。 在 GB300（TP4、GLM-5.2-FP8、MTP）上：相比默认 W8A8，每 token 端到端延迟最高降低 6.8%，相比 #41975 降低 1.9%——同时避免了 #41975 每 GPU +8.2 GiB 的 BF16 权重拷贝。KV pool 保持为 1,196,928 tokens，而非 1,014,848。

  • #44304 — Qwen3.8-Flash-Next gfx950 / MI355X 优化跟踪项。 36 层中的 GatedDeltaNet、12 层中的 QuerySparse Attention、HyperConnection 门控残差、MXFP4 MoE、原生 NEXTN MTP。
  • #45373 — GLM-5.3-Flash Hopper（SM90）优化跟踪项，属于 Q4 内核路线图 #42473 的一部分。
  • #46812 — PD prefill bootstrap 队列前缀现在会在 waiting-prefix LRU 流程中刷新（CLOSED）。 此前，disagg_prefill_bootstrap_queue 中的请求从未被触碰，导致其设备前缀冷却。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. #45755 — Kimi-K3 在 SM90 上：flashinfer_mxfp4 静默计算 GPT-OSS SwiGLU 而非 SiTU。 静默正确性失败——不崩溃，但 token 错误。在 v0.5.22 和 main @ ce66b3ab 上可复现。依赖 flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4209（仍为 open）；此前尝试 #32650 已关闭且未合并。将所有 Kimi-K3 SM90 MXFP4 输出视为可疑。 暂无修复 PR。
  2. #43412 — 投机解码在首个被采样请求上杀死服务器。 在无系统 CUDA toolkit 的 pip 安装包中，flashinfer verify-sampling op 的 JIT 失败（捆绑 cccl 与 pip cu13 toolkit 不匹配），并对进程树执行 SIGKILL。贪心（temp 0）流量不受影响。任何 temp>0 请求都会轻易触发。未引用修复 PR。
  3. #44291 — EP2（tp=2 + ep=2）在 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4、RTX PRO 6000 / sm_120 上出现非法内存访问。 内核级 IMA 在两个构建中均可复现。对于该 checkpoint，sm_120 + Expert Parallel 不可用。
  4. #39300 — TorchNativeAttnBackend 中忽略非因果滑动窗口注意力。 回退后端静默应用因果掩码，导致非因果/SWA 配置产生错误注意力。
  5. #42752 — 测试不稳定与 CI 基础设施故障（134 条评论，最活跃 issue）。 通过 /sglang-pr-babysit 工作流跟踪 NVIDIA PR Test Base / PR Test Extra 的反复不稳定；补充 #17050。高评论量表明 CI 持续不稳定，正在影响合并速度。
  6. #44070 — PD prefill 提前发送缓存前缀可能在 HiCache 回载完成前传输 KV（CLOSED）。 当两个请求共享主机驻留前缀且 SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_EARLY_SEND_CACHED_PREFIX=1（默认）时，Decode 会静默收到陈旧 KV。值得确认修复顺序已落地，因为该 flag 仍默认开启。
  7. #27787 — 使用 moe_runner_backend=flashinfer_trtllm 时 BF16 RL 权重更新崩溃（CLOSED）。 _load_w13 出现 64 与 2048 的形状不匹配；update_weights_from_tensor 路径未恢复填充后的 w13 布局。与 RL 微调循环相关。
  8. #44794 — AMD select_experts 将 fp32 MoE 校正 bias 转换为 bf16（CLOSED）。 尽管 #37133 提供了 fp32 aiter 路径，ROCm 上的 GLM-5.x 仍使用 bf16 bias 进行路由。

同样已关闭、活动较少： #35148（rust sgl-model-gateway 中的 Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 推理解析）、#34969（HF3FS HiCache ZeroDivisionError，DeepSeek-V4）、#35811（HiCache IMA，deepseekv4-flash）、#36598（DSA index_topk override 断言）、#35324（DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 上 DSPARK 的间歇性 CUDA 崩溃）、#36822（BF16 + TP 下 GPTQ Marlin MoE 出现 NaN）、#35702（sharded_state MLA 保存/加载）。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 不要在仅有 pip 的环境中为非贪心流量启用投机解码。 #43412 是硬性杀死进程，而非优雅错误，并且会在首个被采样请求上触发。在问题解决前，要么安装匹配的系统 CUDA toolkit，要么固定使用贪心采样，要么在生产中不启用 spec decode。
  • 在信任 Kimi-K3 SM90 输出前先进行验证。 #45755 是静默的激活函数替换——基准分数和 eval harness 不会将其标记出来。对任何 Hopper 上的 MXFP4 Kimi-K3 部署运行一组已知良好的 prompt 套件。
  • PD 分离在大规模场景下已是默认，而其边缘情况是 KV 正确性 bug，而非性能 bug。 #44070 是一个默认开启的陈旧 KV 风险；如果你运行带 HiCache 的 PD prefill，请确认所用构建包含该修复，并重新运行前缀共享负载。
  • 预期 OpenAI 兼容请求校验会更严格。 #44047 将无效采样边界从“在调度器深处失败”改为“在 API 处拒绝”。审计客户端参数范围，以及任何将 max_completion_tokens=0 作为“未设置”哨兵传递的代码。
  • 按使用方划分的 API key 即将到来（#36666），消除多租户网关共享凭据的变通方案——有助于在不重启的情况下按用户或按服务撤销访问。
  • Agent 工作负载将获得缓存感知路由。 Q4 Agentic Cache Scheduling 路线图（#43098）目标是跨引擎的超级节点级 L1（GPU）+ L2（host）KV 共享，以及感知缓存位置的路由器放置——这一机制可降低长前缀 agent 循环的成本。如果你在共享集群上运行多轮 agent，应为此做规划。
  • RAG/embedding 现已纳入服务层范围，nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B（#45885）原生落地，而不再需要 sidecar。
  • 硬件注意事项： sm_120（RTX PRO 6000）+ EP2 目前对 NVFP4 checkpoint 不可用（#44291）；消费级 Radeon 仍不受支持（#30599）；Apple Silicon 服务仍处于 RFC 阶段（#32321）。
llama.cpp — ggml-org/llama.cpp

llama.cpp 摘要 — 2026-10-28

1. 今日亮点

LiquidAI 的 LFM3 系列强势落地：在 b11938/b11941 中新增四个模型（1.7B、VL-2B、Audio-2B、Omni-2B），此外还有视频输入支持以及 /v1/realtime 上的工具调用（正在评审中）。服务器层还获得了两项值得关注的能力：聊天模板的推理强度等级现在会被探测并暴露（b11944），路由器可通过新的设备内存上限（--models-memory-max，b11930）动态卸载模型。风险方面，量化目标上的投机解码正确性（#25618）仍是讨论最多的未决缺陷，紧随其后的是 sm_120 上的 CUDA graph 挂起。

2. 发布与破坏性变更

  • b11944 — 服务器暴露推理强度等级（#31271）：能力探测现在会为每个候选等级（minimal、low、medium、high、xhigh、max）渲染一个用户轮次，并额外提供一个未知等级对照项，使客户端可以枚举有效的推理强度值。直接解决了 #27455 中由来已久、获得 12 个 👍 的请求（#27455）。
  • b11930 — 新的路由器内存余量：--models-memory-max（#21231）：当模型将超过配置的内存阈值时会动态卸载模型，估算时会纳入待加载模型的大小，并使用 no_alloc 测量需求。这对多模型路由器部署是行为变更——如果你依赖当前常驻集行为，请显式设置此项。
  • b11940 — common 中的延迟工具与 tool_reference 内容部分（#31256）：扩展了工具调用解析面；下游聊天处理程序可能需要处理新的内容部分类型。
  • b11936 — k-pool 稀疏选择与 kq_mask 形状解耦（#31243）：qwen4exp（QSA）和 glm5-next 现在直接索引缓存单元，而不是读取 kq_mask 值。这属于内部改动，但如果你为这些架构维护自定义 kernel，则值得关注。
  • b11935 — RPC 加固（#31204）：在 recv_msg 中捕获 std::length_error，而不是直接终止。
  • 注意：据报告，预构建的 Windows CUDA 二进制文件停留在 b11828，而标签仍在推进——请校验你下载的资产，而不要轻信发布名称。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • LFM3-1.7B 与 LFM3-VL-2B（#31252，b11938）。
  • LFM3-Audio-2B 与 LFM3-Omni-2B（#31257，b11941）——并按发布版本解析 config.json。
  • LiquidAI d1-2B / d1-omni-2B 决策模型（#31275，已合并）。
  • mtmd 中为 LFM3 系列新增视频输入（#31283，待合并）——包含视频+音轨能力矩阵。
  • /v1/realtime 扩展：工具调用（#31287）与语音聊天/交错转写（#31269），二者均面向 LFM3-Audio/Omni GGUFs。
  • GigaChat 3.5 432B-A28B（DeepSeek-V3 风格 MLA + MoE，混合注意力）已在 #25342 中提出。
  • Hexagon 后端：新增 DSV4_HC_PRE/DSV4_HC_POST 算子（#30953）；所有 test-backend-ops 均通过。
  • 后端构建修复：修复 clang-cl + -mavx512bf16 构建（#31276）。
  • 缺口：FP4 量化缺少 round-to-even（#31012）——量化输出与参考舍入结果不同。

4. 性能与优化

  • MoE 专家缓存重构（#31233）：采用受 LRFU/MQ 启发的按类别排序缓存，以衰减的使用历史取代 SLRU。在缓存预热时测得 QFN 上解码 +6%，GLM 上 +7%，专家上传减少 8%。后续改动新增 --moe-cache-cpu-share auto，并为 CPU 未命中引入 CRF 准入（#31286）。
  • Hexagon TOP_K kernel（#31279）：后端采样器曾是 X2 Elite 上最大的草稿阶段开销——占 DFlash 草稿批次的 42%，占 DSpark 的 25%。现在避免了对每个 tile 进行完整排序。
  • cluster 维度变化时重新实例化 CUDA graph（#31284）：Hopper cuBLAS F16 GEMM 会针对不同形状选择不同的线程块 cluster（例如 m=1200 → cluster 5,1,1；m=1040 → 2,2,1）；此前陈旧的 graph 会复用错误的启动配置。
  • SYCL VRAM 超额分配防护（#31285）：拒绝会超出 VRAM 的设备缓冲区，从而避免在 -ngl 999 加载超大模型时发生内核崩溃。
  • 槽位间共享 KV/前缀（#30970）：--slot-attach 允许会话共享由另一个槽位持有的前缀，而不是在缓存中复制一份——对多会话 agent 可显著节省内存。
  • Vulkan MUL_MAT 第 3 维广播（#31239，b11933）：supports_op 不再拒绝所有 ne3 不同的 MUL_MAT；这也解除了 llvmpipe CI 的阻塞。
  • 测试框架提速（#31145，b11934）：save_models 不再构造不需要的 llama_context，缓慢的 std::normal_distribution 抽取已替换为更快的 splitmix 路径。
  • 投机解码 / MTP：通过 d2t 映射为 qwen35/qwen35moe 裁剪草稿词表（#29143）；已卸载的 MTP 层不再计入 GPU 放置数量（#31278）。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. #25618 — 在量化目标上，投机解码在贪婪采样下与常规解码结果不一致（32 条评论）。在 Q4_K_M 等目标上，使用草稿模型投机并设置 temperature=0, top_k=1 时，生成的文本与非投机解码不同，而 bf16 目标则一致。这是影响最大的未决正确性缺陷；尚无修复 PR。
  2. #27330 — CUDA graph 在 RTX 5090 Laptop / sm_120 上挂起 GPU 通道（RC 看门狗 + Xid 8）。已有完整规避方案：GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1。尚无修复 PR。
  3. #29054 — 在 Intel Gen9.5（UHD 630）上使用 q8_0 KV 缓存时，Vulkan GPU 挂起并触发 SIGABRT；vk::Error 逃逸为 std::terminate。可稳定复现。
  4. #27560 — 在 Windows/Vulkan 上使用默认 ctx-checkpoints 时，llama-server 发生访问冲突（0xC0000005）（Qwen3.8-27B）。
  5. #29494 — repeat_last_n / dry_penalty_last_n 无界：会分配数 GB 的零填充采样器内存，导致服务器 OOM。如果将采样器参数暴露给不受信任的客户端，应将其视为 DoS 向量。
  6. #29002 — 混合 LFM2 合批会破坏循环/短卷积状态：在同一个 ubatch 中解码超过 1 个序列会改变输出；贪婪输出可能在一句话中间停止。这与今天落地的 LFM3 混合模型工作直接相关。
  7. #28581 — IQ3_S 在 RTX 5060 Ti（Blackwell）上产生垃圾输出。
  8. #31217 — ggml-rpc 中的 ggml_nbytes() 整数溢出 → 越界读写，可由恶意构造形状的张量触发。修复 PR 已开放；对不受信任的 RPC 对端很重要。
  9. #31220 — aarch64 服务器构建上的投机解码性能下降（回归，尚未确认）。
  10. #31029 — Arrow Lake iGPU 不支持 SYCL bf 转换指令。
  11. #31163 — Vulkan count_experts.comp 的 zero_skipped_rows() 中，每个线程都会遍历每一个 expert id（源自 #26631 的性能缺陷）。
  12. 今日修复：mtmd-cli 在 /clear 后批次陈旧（#31155）→ 在 b11932 中缩小了批次指针作用域（#31165）；DSV4.1 GSQ-RCO 加载失败（#31263）已关闭；Vulkan Navi 10 GPU ring 挂起（#28807、#28808）已作为陈旧问题关闭。另请注意，update_slots() 未将 batch_view 偏移传播到 ctx_dft 的问题已关闭（#24840）。
  13. 工具/CI：MSVC 无法检测 AVX-VNNI（#28295），并且 json-schema-to-grammar 会逐字复制原始控制字节，在 schema 模式中出现 NUL 时出错——修复见 #31241，如果你接受用户提供的 JSON schema，这一点很重要。

6. 这对应用开发者意味着什么

  • 推理强度现在可被发现，而不再靠猜。 b11944 的探测让客户端可以询问服务器，已加载的聊天模板实际支持哪些等级（minimal…max），从而将应用层的“思考预算”映射到模板支持的值，而不是发出模型会静默忽略的等级。设计截断 UI 时，可结合已关闭的优雅预算请求（#20632）。
  • Agent 的工具链路更完善。 tool_reference 内容部分与延迟工具（b11940），加上 /v1/realtime 工具调用（#31287），意味着 OpenAI 形态的工具循环现在可以横跨文本、音频和视频输入，而无需旁路通道。在推进上线前，请验证你的解析器能处理新的内容部分类型。
  • 借助 LFM3-Audio/Omni-2B 与实时转写端点，语音/全模态 agent 在 CPU 级硬件上已可行——但在 #29002 解决前，避免对混合 LFM 模型的多个序列进行合批；请将这些会话串行化，或使用独立上下文。
  • 多租户模型路由器应采用 --models-memory-max（b11930）。它把硬 OOM 失败转化为确定性的驱逐，但会改变常驻语义——请审计任何假设热模型会保持加载的延迟 SLO。
  • 不要在没有与常规解码进行输出一致性测试的情况下，发布使用量化草稿/目标对的投机解码（#25618）。在 sm_120（RTX 50 系列）主机上，请设置 GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1，直到 #27330 落地。
  • 在服务端为采样器参数设置上限。 无界的 repeat_last_n/dry_penalty_last_n（#29494）会让单个请求分配数 GB 内存——每个托管部署今天都应添加这一行校验。
  • 固定并校验二进制文件。 Windows CUDA 预构建版本停留在 b11828（#31085），意味着“最新发布”并不是“最新代码”的可靠代名词——请检查内嵌的构建号；如果你需要今天的 LFM3 或推理强度变更，请自行构建。
Ollama — ollama/ollama

Ollama 摘要 — 2026-10-28

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有版本发布。活动集中在模型接入与运行时加固上：LFM3 支持正在 PR #19344 中修复，此前用户遇到了 issue #19347 和 issue #19343；与此同时，MLX 在 PR #19197 中获得并发生成支持，CUDA 启动崩溃缓解在 PR #18978 中。高影响未解决问题仍集中在云端推理循环 #17892、Qwen3.8 工具循环 500 #17778 以及 macOS Metal/MLX 崩溃 #19278、#18885。

2. 发布与破坏性变更

过去 24 小时无新版本发布，也没有确认的 API/配置破坏性变更。兼容性工作正在进行但尚未发布：流式错误转发 PR #18953、Anthropic 思考块流式传输 PR #19110，以及 OpenAI 开发者指令处理 PR #19199（已关闭）。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • LFM3 GGUF 修复 — PR #19344（开放）修复 LFM3 GGUF 的 BOS 处理，并新增 GGUF 文本转语音支持；解决 issue #19347（unknown model architecture: 'lfm3'，已关闭）和 issue #19343（MLX 运行时不可用）。
  • Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B — PR #19229（开放）添加逐层专家配置、LiLiCorr 推测解码、预量化 affine 3-bit 导入以及混合精度专家堆叠。
  • Kolibri 1 — PR #18780（开放）添加 MLX 支持。
  • MLX 并发生成 — PR #19197（开放）通过 OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL 支持多个同时生成请求。
  • CUDA/Blackwell 启动 — PR #18978（开放）使用 eager CUDA 模块加载重试 llama-server 启动，针对 RTX 5060 Ti/Blackwell 上的共享对象初始化失败；关联到 issue #19122。
  • GPU 发现修复 — PR #19338（开放）修正对支持所有 GPU 的最新库版本的选择。
  • 仅功能请求 — 桌面 UI 中的 GPU 加速检测 issue #19301；AMD RX 6750 GRE 10GB 支持 issue #19329。

4. 性能与优化

  • MLX 并行 — PR #19197 允许 MLX 模型并发处理多个请求，降低排队请求的首 token 时间。默认仍为一个请求；必须为每个活跃请求预留内存。
  • CUDA 启动重试 — PR #18978 通过 eager 模块加载缓解部分卸载预热崩溃。未提供吞吐量数据。
  • 调度器驱逐 — issue #19326 报告 findRunnerToUnload 先按 sessionDuration、再按模型路径排序；当 keep_alive 一致时，驱逐会变得任意，而不是基于大小/最近使用。未列出修复 PR。
  • OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1 语义 — issue #19262 报告尽管设置了该值，仍有两个会话并发运行。未列出修复 PR。
  • Vulkan 回归 — issue #13567（已关闭）报告 gpt-oss 在 Vulkan 上相比 CPU/llama.cpp 较慢；所提供数据中没有修复详情。

5. 稳定性与回归

高严重性

  • macOS Metal 崩溃 / MLX panic — issue #19278 报告在 Ollama 0.40.9 上出现 mlx runner failed: panic: mlx: [METAL] Command buffer execution failed；issue #18885 报告 gemma4:e2b-mlx 上出现 MLX runner panic。未列出修复 PR。
  • CUDA 共享对象初始化失败 — issue #19122 出现在 Windows 上的 RTX 5060 Ti/Blackwell、部分卸载场景。修复 PR PR #18978 处于开放状态。
  • 云端思考循环 — issue #17892：deepseek-v4-flash:0731 在约 1 分 45 秒内重复同一推理块 221 次，且没有任何可用输出。未列出修复 PR。
  • Qwen3.8 工具循环 500 — issue #17778：工具调用循环期间出现 ResponseError during chat streaming: no user query found in messages；56 条评论，未列出修复 PR。
  • Windows 连接重置 — issue #19139：在 Windows/RTX 3090 上，大提示词会使 /api/chat 在约 15 秒后重置；标记为需要更多信息。
  • 拉取恢复损坏 — issue #19337：在拉取开始超过一小时后重启服务器，会因部分文件缺失或摘要不匹配而破坏恢复。修复 PR PR #19339 处于开放状态。
  • 工具调用被静默丢弃 — issue #19187：对不在请求 tools 中的函数的调用会被静默丢弃，产生空响应且 eval_count > 0。未列出修复 PR。
  • 低比特 Qwen2.5-Coder 产物损坏 — issue #18252：qwen2.5-coder:3b-instruct 的 q2_K/q3_K_S/q3_K_M/q3_K_L 在功能冒烟测试套件中得分为 0/15，而同系列量化版本通过率为 87–100%。未列出修复 PR。

中等严重性

  • OpenAI 工具调用错误附加 — issue #19151（已关闭）：当 content: [] 时，助手的 tool_calls 被附加到上一条消息。
  • 云端 Responses 413 — issue #19155（已关闭）：约 10.7 MiB 的编码请求被拒绝，尽管低于宣称的上下文限制。
  • /v1/systemone 决策模型 — issue #19292：自 0.40.4 起，带有 CAPABILITY decision 但没有 decision.type 的 GGUF 模型会被拒绝。
  • DNS64 拉取失败 — issue #19345：在 DNS64 环境下，ollama pull hf.co/... 失败，因为 NAT64 CDN 地址被视为非公网地址。
  • LFM3 运行时不匹配 — issue #19343：lfm3-audio:latest 需要不可用的 MLX 支持；issue #19347（已关闭）在修复 PR 之前报告了未知的 lfm3 架构。
  • 调度器驱逐行为 — issue #19326：当 keep_alive 相同时，模型驱逐变得任意。

低严重性

  • Modelfile 往返 bug — issue #19342：当值包含后跟空白的 """ 时，ollama show --modelfile 会输出无法解析的内容。
  • REPL 状态 bug — issue #19340：在多行输入期间按 Ctrl+C 会使 REPL 停留在多行模式；issue #19341：/load 不能一致地重置系统提示词。
  • ShieldGemma 模板 — issue #19313：模板在应用于用户提示词时会分类出“an AI response”。

6. 这对应用开发者意味着什么

  • 锁定版本并分阶段升级。 在 #19278、#18885 和 #19122 解决之前，避免统一采用 0.40.x MLX 或 Blackwell CUDA 配置。
  • 为云端推理模型添加循环和超时检测。 #17892 可能消耗数分钟且不产生输出；强制执行最大推理/token 预算，并用其他模型重试。
  • 防御性地校验工具调用。 未知工具名称可能被静默丢弃（#19187）；检查 eval_count 非零的空响应。不要假设 tool_calls 在空内容数组后仍然保留（#19151）。
  • 处理带内流式错误。 在 PR #18953 发布之前，客户端在首个 token 之后可能收到空白块，而不是传播的错误。
  • 为 MLX 并发预留内存。 PR #19197 可通过 OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL 改善 TTFT，但每个并行请求都需要额外内存。
  • 避免已知有问题的量化。 不要在代码任务中使用 qwen2.5-coder:3b-instruct 的 q2_K/q3_K_* 变体；使用更高比特的同系列版本（#18252）。
  • 让拉取可恢复且可安全重启。 添加重试逻辑，并在 PR #19339 合入之前避免在拉取过程中重启 ollama serve（#19337）。
  • 显式控制模型驻留。 当 keep_alive 一致时，调度器驱逐可能按模型路径而不是最近使用情况选择（#19326）；设置差异化的 keep_alive 值或预加载关键模型。
  • 私有 OCI 仓库仍是缺口。 启用认证的拉取/推送仍在 #9215 和 #4204 中被请求；在隔离网络/私有部署中需要围绕这一点做规划。

⚠️ 安全回移植待完成： #47904 (OPEN) — 所有已发布的 1.106.x 镜像仍信任 emSign ECC Root CA - G3。截至今日，#47670 中的修复仅存在于 main。如果你在 1.106.x 上使用出站 TLS，请密切关注。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • Databricks OpenJev 决策模型定价 — #48694：databricks/databricks-openjev-qwen35-4b 此前映射为 0.0 成本，因此所有 /v1/decisions 和 /v1/systemone 调用都记录为 $0 花费。现在按 Databricks 公布的 每 100 万输入 token 0.6 DBU（$0.070/DBU）计价。
  • Cloudflare Workers AI 扩展（仍未合并） — #21115 (OPEN，陈旧)：提供商实现比 Cloudflare 扩展后的 API 落后约 10 个月。图像支持（#35055）和音频/STT/TTS 支持（#35056）的配套功能请求仍处于 OPEN 且陈旧状态。
  • Tavily 搜索透传 — #48684 (OPEN)：现在转发 raw_content、score、favicon 以及响应信封。此前调用方为 include_raw_content 付费，却只收到 title/url/excerpt。
  • 透传模型归因 — #48275 (CLOSED)：上游可以通过 x-litellm-upstream-model 报告模型，因此没有 model 字段的产品端点不再归入 unknown 花费桶。
  • SAP 工具调用重放 — #48696 (OPEN)：重放的 assistant 工具调用若省略 arguments，现在会发送空字符串，而不是在本地失败。

本时间窗口内没有新的 CUDA/ROCm/Metal 后端或量化格式。

4. 性能与优化

  • 仅请求侧护栏的流式快速路径已恢复 — #47735 (OPEN)：仅提示词护栏此前会强制对每个流式回复做逐块响应检查，就每一段询问护栏。现在除非确有组件检查流式块，否则跳过该检查。对位于护栏后的流有显著延迟收益。
  • 多模态配额估算 — #48099 (OPEN)：图片较多的 Responses 请求此前按文本计数并触发 token 限制拒绝，而 Chat 图片/音频请求预留不足。媒体现在单独估算（图像模型策略、音频时长），并在各代理路径间共享。
  • Rust 桥接层改为强制 — #46346 (OPEN)：_native 已随每个 wheel 发布，且 sdist 没有它就无法安装；此改动移除了可选加载路径和无用的 None 分支。基于 #46442 叠加，后者为 CI 缓存 Rust 构建。
  • 嵌入超时传播 — #48690 (CLOSED) / #47305 (CLOSED)：Gemini 和 Vertex 的 embed_content 同步/异步路径忽略了调用方超时，使用 300 秒处理器默认值——50 毫秒超时仍在约 1 秒后返回真实嵌入。现在会正确转发（批处理处理器也一样）。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序。

严重

  • 🔴 1.106.x 镜像仍信任已失陷的根 CA — #47904 (OPEN)。修复仅存在于 main。尚无回移植 PR。

高 — 计费正确性

  • 🟠 当 provider_response_model 是价格映射中不存在的 slug（例如带日期的 Anthropic 构建）时，流式请求按 $0 计费 — #42161 (CLOSED)。报告者看到 89 次可计费调用中有 74 次被记录为免费；非流式计费正确。修复已合入。
  • 🟠 虚拟密钥 BudgetExceededError 使用过期花费，而 /key/info 报告的花费低于 max_budget — #27735 (OPEN，12 条评论，当日讨论最多的 issue)。与 #27639 相关；影响团队范围的虚拟密钥。
  • 🟠 当 /v1/messages 携带 Anthropic 格式的 tool_choice（{"type":"auto"|"any"|"tool"}）时，预算预留会因 token_counter KeyError 而按 max_input_tokens 确定大小 — #47396 (CLOSED)。导致预留膨胀 / 误拒绝。
  • 🟠 自 v1.99.0 起，对于返回 id: null 的提供商（Databricks-Gemini），SpendLogs 被静默丢弃 — request_id 变为 "None" 并在主键上冲突 — #39749 (CLOSED)。
  • 🟡 当数据库会话时区 ≠ UTC 时，SpendLogs 分区边界错位 — #34364 (OPEN，增强项)。

高 — 资源泄漏 / 路由

  • 🟠 websearch_interception 对每个携带 web_search 工具的流式 /v1/messages 请求泄漏一个 max_parallel_requests 槽位 — #46093 (CLOSED)。v3 限流器的调用前钩子获取该槽位；智能体循环从不释放它，永久缩小密钥容量。
  • 🟡 基于路由器冷却状态的结构化提供商错误 / 路由健康契约 — #33371 (OPEN，RFC)。冷却状态在内部存在，但不可机读。

中 — 协议/转换

  • 🟡 通过 Chat Completions 适配器流式传输时，/v1/messages 适配器发出的 message_start 中 usage.input_tokens: 0（四项 usage 计数全为零） — #48481 (CLOSED)。真实计数仅在 message_delta 中到达；非流式正确。会破坏客户端的早期 token 记账。
  • 🟡 在默认开启思考的 Claude 模型（例如 anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5）上，reasoning_effort: "none" 会移除思考配置，而不是禁用它 — #47924 (OPEN)。上游默认值生效；目前无法强制关闭思考。
  • 🟡 Responses 适配器中围绕 tool_use 的 assistant 文本顺序丢失 — [text, tool_use, text] 变成 [function_call, message(text+text)]，在调用之后重放工具调用前的文本 — #45478 (OPEN)。
  • 🟡 格式错误的 Messages tool_choice 返回 500 或静默变为 auto — #46188 (OPEN)。现在以 400 拒绝；有意的产品变更。
  • 🟡 Decisions 转换将省略的概率实体化为 0.0 — #48449 (CLOSED)。缺失 ≠ 零；信息丢失。
  • 🟡 Responses 流式传输在省略 logprobs 时中断（event.part.text 上的 AttributeError）— #48375、#48686 (CLOSED)。

中 — 代理/API 行为

  • 🟡 来自 #46839 的 token 计数输入优先级回归 — 当 prompt 与非空 messages/contents 同时出现时，现在会返回 400，除非开启 drop_params — #48693 (OPEN，恢复旧有优先级)。
  • 🟡 BYOK / 静态认证 MCP tools/list 拒绝每请求的 x-mcp-{alias}-authorization — #46664 (OPEN)。
  • 🟡 **非对象 JSON 请求体（[]、123、null）在 pre_db_read_auth_checks 中返回 500 而不是 400 — #43711 (CLOSED，AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get')。
  • 🟡 仅企业版可用的 get_spend_routes 权限在 /key/generate 和 /user/new 上产生裸 500；许可证消息仅进入日志 — #47011 (CLOSED)。
  • 🟡 mock_response="" 为假值 → 在 completion()/acompletion() 中触发真实提供商请求 — #48162 (CLOSED)。测试安全性隐患：空 mock 字符串泄漏了真实流量。
  • 🟡 hide-secrets 护栏忽略了 skip_tool_message_in_guardrail — #48689 (OPEN)。尽管有该标志，工具结果仍被擦除；工具参数/用户文本/系统提示词仍被脱敏。

低 — UI / 可观测性

  • #23998 (CLOSED) — 在 UI 中添加 LiteLLM Params 后无法移除。
  • #32332 (CLOSED) — 当 request_id 包含 # 时，Logs UI 显示 "Request/Response Data Not Available"。
  • #34763 (CLOSED) — MCP 服务器 UI 省略 authorization 认证类型，尽管 API 接受它。
  • #35064 (OPEN，陈旧) — 在 UI 中找不到 enable_background_health_checks。
  • #33690 (CLOSED) — 文档中 SSO 角色值不匹配（internal_user_view_only 与 internal_user_viewer）。
  • #19730 (OPEN，15 👍) — i18n / 多语言仪表盘，仍是最高赞的开启请求。
  • #48688 (OPEN) — 护栏向导导航按钮溢出对话框。
  • #48600 (OPEN) — LITELLM_FIPS_MODE=true 启动门禁；除非 FIPS 加密 + TLS 验证实际启用，否则拒绝启动。用修正后的探针重做已回滚的 #42700。
  • #42697 (OPEN) — 启用 LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true 时，key/user/team/org 身份现在作为一等 Langfuse 元数据字段在 chat、/v1/messages 和 /v1/responses 上发出，而不是原始属性 blob。
  • #34734 (OPEN) — SDK 中基于能力的上游配额/余额探测。

6. 这对应用开发者意味着什么

  1. 在信任仪表盘之前审计流式花费。 两个独立缺陷（#42161、#39749）导致流式调用记录为 $0 或完全消失。如果你将大部分流量走流式——尤其是通过 Databricks/Gemini 或带日期的 Anthropic 模型 slug——在修复传播到你固定的版本之前，请将 SpendLogs 与提供商发票对账。
  2. 固定版本并验证，不要浮动。 四条并行补丁线已上线，且 1.108.0 是 RC 而不是稳定标签。使用上述 cosign 命令，并将 1.106.x 视为有安全标记，直到 eMudhra 根 CA 回移植落地（#47904）。
  3. /v1/messages 仍是变动最频繁的接口面。 工具调用排序（#45478）、格式错误的 tool_choice 现在返回 400（#46188）、message_start usage 归零（#48481），以及使用 Anthropic tool_choice 时的预算过度预留（#47396）都涉及 Anthropic 兼容路径。流式使用工具的 agent 应显式针对固定版本进行测试。
  4. 流式容量可能静默侵蚀。 web_search 槽位泄漏（#46093）会为每个受影响的流永久消耗 max_parallel_requests——如果长期存活的密钥在数小时内性能下降，请回收它，并在扩容前检查此类泄漏。
  5. 护栏延迟税正在消失。 如果你因延迟而禁用流式或放弃护栏，#47735 为仅提示词护栏恢复了流式快速路径。同样，嵌入超时现在真正生效（#48690）——请移除任何客户端超时规避方案。
  6. 不要依赖 mock_response=""。 它会路由到真实提供商（#48162）。在测试中使用非空哨兵值或 mock_tool_calls/mock_timeout。
  7. FIPS 和 OTEL v2 为可选启用，但正在落地。 #48600 提供失败关闭的 FIPS 启动检查；#42697 在 OTEL v2 映射器下使每请求身份可在 Langfuse 中查询——如果你正在为多租户 agent 流量做埋点，这会很有用。
Unsloth — unslothai/unsloth

Unsloth 摘要 — 2026-10-28

今日要闻

过去 24 小时内没有新版本发布；活动集中在 Unsloth Studio 的加固和正确性修复上。影响最大的事项包括：一个 Windows 桌面端训练 bug 会向回收站灌入大量 SQLite WAL/SHM 文件；一个 Anthropic 兼容性回归，/v1/messages 返回硬性上下文溢出错误而不是自动压缩；以及针对 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 的两项 FP8/Block Swap 修复。模型支持需求正转向非 NVIDIA 硬件（Intel Arc XPU、NVIDIA/AMD 混合 Linux）和新的 LiquidAI LFM3 系列。

新模型与硬件支持

  • LFM3 系列请求 — #15588 请求在 LiquidAI 发布 LFM3 后支持 LFM3-1.7B（2 👍）。尚无实现 PR。
  • Intel Arc B580 (XPU) 微调 — #15583 报告称 Windows 11 上的桌面应用未提供 Intel XPU 训练路径。仍处于打开状态，有 5 条评论；未关联后端 PR。
  • NVIDIA/AMD 混合 Linux 上 AMD GPU 不可见 — #15444 显示 Studio Web UI 无法在存在 NVIDIA 卡时枚举 AMD 设备，具体是在 Kali 上使用自定义 llama.cpp 构建时。这对异构推理主机很重要。
  • ExLlamaV3 作为推理引擎 — #15527 请求支持 exllamav3 和 EXL3 量化排序；请求者指出现有社区 PR 已停滞，因此不会很快实现。
  • Apple MLX 上的 Gemma 4 26B（视觉） — #15473 报告称视觉路径在 macOS 27.1 / MLX 上输出 <unused6226> token，即分词器或多模态投影器不匹配，而不是缺少架构。
  • Qwen3.8-Flash-Next（FP8，qwen4_exp） — 加载缺陷追踪于 #15632 和 #15633；这现在是仓库中修补最活跃的新架构。

性能与优化

  • Block Swap 的 offload_layers 在 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 上从未生效 — #15633：CPU 驻留的 n-gram 表使设备映射看起来像两个设备，因此层卸载被静默跳过。配套修复位于 #15632（FP8 n-gram 表缺少 weight_scale，导致 FP8 输入进入 key_proj）和 unsloth-zoo#36（该表被排除在 Block Swap 的槽池之外）。合并来看，这些问题同时影响 FP8 Flash-Next 的显存占用和数值正确性。
  • 基准测试页面工作正在进行中 — #11808 针对已加载的 GGUF 扫描投机解码（MTP、n-gram、DSpark、DFlash）、草稿 token 数、KV 缓存类型、上下文长度、并行槽和 RAM 卸载；#12522 添加用于 pp/tg 吞吐量的 llama-bench 标签页；#12521 添加按量化分组的 lm-eval-harness 评分。这些是调优服务配置时缺失的测量界面。
  • 实时监控重做 — #15630 将内存报告合并为单个统一内存行，并新增刷新率设置；现有的大小调整手柄无法使用。
  • 可观测性缺口已确认 — #14582 请求在详细 UI 中显示预填充/加载进度、专家/层卸载量以及实时解码/预填充速度。目前这些数字只能通过上面的基准测试 PR 推断。

稳定性与回归

按对生产用户的严重程度排序：

  1. Windows 上 Studio 训练灌满回收站 — #15552：*.db-wal / *.db-shm 文件大约每秒写入一次 C:\$Recycle.Bin\<SID>\；90 分钟的运行会产生 >10,000 个条目（~40 MB）。存在磁盘耗尽风险，并且在端点安全软件看来类似恶意软件。尚无修复 PR。
  2. Anthropic 透传忽略自动压缩 — #15417：当历史超过 n_ctx 时，/v1/messages 返回不可恢复的 400 exceed_context_size_error，即使已启用自动压缩。这会直接破坏 Claude-SDK 风格的客户端。尚无修复 PR。
  3. 每个会话残留磁盘占用 — #14487：每次使用桌面端后 C: 盘会损失 200–400 MB，且没有清理路径；自 2026-10-21 起处于打开状态。
  4. Studio 训练期间出现堆栈跟踪 — #15538：Studio Web UI 训练路径上出现未处理异常。
  5. Deep Research 未被调用 — #15581：Gemma-4-26B-A4B 忽略 Deep Research 工具并从权重作答，即工具选择/路由失败，而不是检索失败。
  6. MLX 视觉 token 损坏 — #15473（见上文）；输出静默出错，对下游解析来说比崩溃更糟。

过去 24 小时内已解决：

  • SGLang 自动压缩已修复 — #15434（已关闭）：托管 SGLang 引擎上的长聊天此前在一次超上下文请求后会永久卡住。
  • Qwen3.5-2B 分片权重恢复功能损坏 — #15405（已关闭）：_MODEL_WEIGHT_RE 无法匹配 model.safetensors-00001-of-00001.safetensors。
  • 破坏性“清除全部”转录记录 — #15570（已关闭）：桌面端跳过了浏览器构建中已有的确认对话框。
  • macOS Flux-3 图像编辑 — #15241（已关闭）。

CI/工具链：#15626 阻止 pytest 9.2 的 monkeypatch 删除 torch._dynamo.config 条目（间歇性后端 CI 失败）；#15622 修复 verify_import_hoist.py 的误报，这些误报目前阻塞两个重构 PR。

这对应用开发者意味着什么

  • 对于 Anthropic 兼容客户端，不要依赖服务端上下文管理。 在 #15417 落地之前，请在调用 /v1/messages 前自行执行 token 预算和截断；失败模式是 400，而不是透明压缩。
  • MCP 工具定义开销现在是一项真实的上下文成本。 根据 #15629 / #15631，Studio 的 MCP 服务器暴露 23 个工具，在任何工作开始前就消耗 ~18k token 的定义。按工具开关是预期的缓解措施——只启用智能体所需的内容。
  • 运行时模型发现将通过 OpenCode 提供 — #15521 跟踪一个上游插件，使 unsloth start opencode 用户可以在运行时枚举 Studio 模型，而无需硬编码端点。
  • 量化选择仍然是隐式的。 #14362 指出，未显式指定量化的 API 请求会回退到模型默认值（例如 UD-Q5_K_XL），无法设置偏好的默认值（如 Q8_0）——如果可复现性很重要，请在请求中显式固定量化。
  • 缺少带宽控制 — #15603 请求增加下载速率限制；这对拉取许多 GGUF 变体的共享 CI 运行器和预配流水线很有意义。
  • 硬件指引： Intel XPU 和 NVIDIA/AMD 混合 Linux 目前仍不受支持/无法检测（#15583、#15444）；ExLlamaV3 不是可用后端（#15527）。请围绕 NVIDIA CUDA、单一厂商 ROCm 或 Apple MLX 规划部署。
  • 在空间受限的系统盘上，避免长时间运行 Windows 桌面端训练，直到 #15552 修复；训练期间监控 C:\$Recycle.Bin 的增长。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-10-28

Generated: 2026-10-28 01:35 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project AI Infrastructure Comparison — 2026-10-28

Scope: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, LiteLLM, Unsloth.
n/r = not reported in the supplied 24h digest. SGLang is the only project with explicit 24h issue/PR counts.

1. Ecosystem Overview

The ecosystem is in a hardware-qualification and correctness-hardening phase rather than a major release phase. Serving engines are racing to cover DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.8, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.x and new accelerator targets such as SM120, ROCm MI355X and GB300, but several high-severity issues are silent-correctness or process-kill bugs rather than throughput regressions. Local runtimes are absorbing the new LiquidAI LFM3 family quickly, especially llama.cpp, while Ollama follows with fixes and MLX concurrency work. The gateway layer is shipping patches but still carries a security backport gap and billing-correctness issues. Fine-tuning tooling is focused on Studio hardening and FP8/Block Swap fixes, with new-model support lagging the serving engines.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues count (24h) PR count (24h) Release status Activity signal
vLLM n/r n/r No releases; no breaking changes Hardware/model coverage plus critical regressions. #50576 has 121 comments; #56892 is a critical SM120 CUDA-graph/decode issue.
SGLang 63 updated 500 updated No releases Roadmap/tracker consolidation and a large [inactive] stale sweep. Critical spec-decode crash #43412 and silent Kimi-K3 SM90 bug #45755.
llama.cpp n/r n/r Continuous builds b11930–b11944; no formal release LFM3 family landed across text/vision/audio/omni; reasoning-effort discovery and router memory ceiling shipped.
Ollama n/r n/r No releases LFM3 GGUF fixes, MLX concurrent generation, CUDA/Blackwell startup mitigation. Multiple unresolved macOS/MLX and tool-loop issues.
LiteLLM n/r n/r 4 patch releases: v1.106.5, v1.105.6, v1.104.8, v1.103.10; main on 1.109.0; 1.108.0 as RC Security backport outstanding for 1.106.x images; multiple streaming/billing and slot-leak fixes.
Unsloth n/r n/r No releases Studio hardening; FP8/Block Swap fixes for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; Windows Recycle Bin and Anthropic auto-compaction regressions.

3. Model Support Race

Project New model / architecture support today Assessment

6. Trend Signals

  • Hardware-quantization qualification is now a first-class production task. DeepSeek-V4-Flash is still missing on SM8x, SM120 CUDA graphs are broken for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, sm_120 + EP2 is unusable for some NVFP4 checkpoints, and Intel XPU / mixed NVIDIA-AMD / consumer Radeon remain gaps. Treat hardware + model + quant as a tested tuple, not a generic “CUDA” or “ROCm” target.
  • Correctness bugs are outpacing performance wins in risk. SGLang’s Kimi-K3 SM90 MXFP4 silently computes the wrong activation, llama.cpp speculative decoding diverges on quantized targets, vLLM greedy output can change across restarts, and SGLang PD prefill had a stale-KV hazard. Output-equality and prefix-sharing regression tests should gate upgrades.
  • Speculative decoding and MoE remain high-leverage but high-risk. vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama and Unsloth all touch draft models, MTP, expert caches or spec-decode paths today. The pattern is consistent: large potential gains, but crashes, hangs, silent divergence or accuracy collapse appear around quantized/MoE/PD configurations.
  • PD disaggregation and cache-aware routing are moving toward default architecture for agents. SGLang’s PD and agentic-cache roadmaps, vLLM’s KV offload RFCs, and llama.cpp prefix sharing all target the same problem: long-prefix, multi-turn agent loops are expensive, so KV locality and cache routing become control-plane concerns.
  • Agent/tooling compatibility is fragmenting. vLLM’s Rust frontend can 500 on auto tool parsers; Ollama has tool-loop 500s and silent tool-call drops; LiteLLM’s /v1/messages path is the highest-churn surface; llama.cpp is adding tool_reference and realtime tool calls. Application developers should validate tool-call ordering, empty-content handling, unknown-tool behavior and parameter bounds against pinned versions.
  • Supply-chain and DoS hardening are back on the agenda. LiteLLM 1.106.x images still trust a compromised root CA, llama.cpp has an open RPC ggml_nbytes() overflow fix, and unbounded sampler parameters can trigger multi-GB allocations. Gateway and server deployments need cosign verification, input caps and untrusted-peer assumptions.
  • Local multimodal and voice agents are becoming practical. LFM3 text/vision/audio/omni support in llama.cpp, Ollama’s MLX work, and realtime transcription/tool-call endpoints point to local agents that span text, audio and video. Watch co-batching and hybrid-state correctness issues before scaling multi-session local deployments.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Do not enable speculative decoding on non-greedy traffic in pip-only environments. #43412 is a hard process kill, not a graceful error, and it triggers on the first sampled request. Until resolved, either install a matching system CUDA toolkit, pin to greedy sampling, or run without spec decode in production.
  • Validate Kimi-K3 SM90 outputs before trusting them. #45755 is a silent activation-function substitution — benchmark scores and eval harnesses will not flag it. Run a known-good prompt suite against any MXFP4 Kimi-K3 deployment on Hopper.
  • PD disaggregation is the default at scale, and its edge cases are KV-correctness bugs, not perf bugs. #44070 is a stale-KV hazard that was on by default; if you operate PD prefill with HiCache, verify you are on a build containing the fix and re-run prefix-sharing workloads.
  • Expect stricter OpenAI-compat request validation. #44047 moves invalid sampling bounds from "fails deep in the scheduler" to "rejected at the API." Audit client-side parameter ranges and any code passing max_completion_tokens=0 as an "unset" sentinel.
  • Per-consumer API keys are coming (#36666), removing the shared-credential workaround for multi-tenant gateways — useful for revoking access per user or per service without a restart.
  • Agent workloads get cache-aware routing. The Q4 Agentic Cache Scheduling roadmap (#43098) targets supernode-wide L1 (GPU) + L2 (host) KV sharing across engines plus cache-location-aware router placement — the mechanism that makes long-prefix agent loops cheap. Plan for it if you run multi-turn agents against a shared cluster.
  • RAG/embedding is now in scope for the serving layer, with nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B (#45885) landing natively rather than requiring a sidecar.
  • Hardware caveats: sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000) + EP2 is currently broken for NVFP4 checkpoints (#44291); consumer Radeon remains unsupported (#30599); Apple Silicon serving is still at RFC stage (#32321).

  • MoE expert cache rework (#31233): LRFU/MQ-inspired class-ranked cache replacing SLRU with decaying usage history. Measured +6% decode on QFN, +7% on GLM, 8% fewer expert uploads with a warm cache. A follow-up adds --moe-cache-cpu-share auto with CRF admission for CPU misses (#31286).
  • Hexagon TOP_K kernel (#31279): backend sampler was the largest draft cost on X2 Elite — 42% of the DFlash draft batch, 25% of DSpark. Now avoids full per-tile sorting.
  • CUDA graph re-instantiation on cluster-dim changes (#31284): Hopper cuBLAS F16 GEMMs pick different thread-block clusters per shape (e.g. m=1200 → cluster 5,1,1; m=1040 → 2,2,1); stale graphs previously reused the wrong launch config.
  • SYCL VRAM overcommit guard (#31285): refuses device buffers that would exceed VRAM, avoiding kernel panics on -ngl 999 with oversize models.
  • KV/prefix sharing between slots (#30970): --slot-attach lets sessions share a prefix held by another slot instead of duplicating it in cache — meaningful memory savings for multi-session agents.
  • Vulkan MUL_MAT dim-3 broadcast (#31239, b11933): supports_op no longer rejects all MUL_MAT with differing ne3; also unblocks llvmpipe CI.
  • Test harness speedup (#31145, b11934): save_models no longer constructs an unneeded llama_context, and slow std::normal_distribution draws were replaced with a faster splitmix path.
  • Speculative decoding / MTP: draft-vocabulary trim via d2t mapping for qwen35/qwen35moe (#29143); unloaded MTP layers excluded from GPU placement counts (#31278).

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. #25618 — Speculative decoding diverges from vanilla under greedy sampling on quantized targets (32 comments). temperature=0, top_k=1 with draft-model speculation produces different text than non-speculative on Q4_K_M etc., while bf16 targets match. Highest-impact open correctness bug; no fix PR yet.
  2. #27330 — CUDA graphs hang the GPU channel on RTX 5090 Laptop / sm_120 (RC watchdog + Xid 8). Workaround is complete: GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1. No fix PR.
  3. #29054 — Vulkan GPU hang + SIGABRT on Intel Gen9.5 (UHD 630) with q8_0 KV cache; vk::Error escapes as std::terminate. Deterministic.
  4. #27560 — llama-server access violation (0xC0000005) on Windows/Vulkan with default ctx-checkpoints (Qwen3.8-27B).
  5. #29494 — repeat_last_n / dry_penalty_last_n unbounded: multi-GB zero-filled sampler allocations, server OOM. Treat as a DoS vector if exposing sampler params to untrusted clients.
  6. #29002 — Hybrid LFM2 co-batching corrupts recurrent/short-conv state: decoding >1 sequence in the same ubatch changes output; greedy output can stop mid-sentence. Directly relevant to the LFM3 hybrid work landing today.
  7. #28581 — IQ3_S produces garbage on RTX 5060 Ti (Blackwell).
  8. #31217 — ggml_nbytes() integer overflow in ggml-rpc → OOB read/write with maliciously shaped tensors. Fix PR open; relevant for untrusted RPC peers.
  9. #31220 — Speculative decode performance drop on aarch64 server builds (regression, unconfirmed).
  10. #31029 — SYCL bf conversion instruction unsupported on Arrow Lake iGPU.
  11. #31163 — Vulkan count_experts.comp zero_skipped_rows() loops over every expert id per thread (perf bug from #26631).
  12. Fixed today: mtmd-cli stale batch after /clear (#31155) → reduced batch-pointer scope in b11932 (#31165); DSV4.1 GSQ-RCO load failure (#31263) closed; Vulkan Navi 10 GPU ring hangs (#28807, #28808) closed stale. Also note update_slots() not propagating batch_view offset to ctx_dft was closed (#24840).
  13. Tooling/CI: MSVC doesn't detect AVX-VNNI (#28295), and json-schema-to-grammar copies raw control bytes verbatim, breaking on NUL in schema patterns — fix in #31241, which matters if you accept user-supplied JSON schemas.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Reasoning effort is now discoverable, not guessed. The b11944 probe lets your client ask the server which levels (minimal…max) the loaded chat template actually honors, so you can map app-level "thinking budget" to template-supported values instead of emitting levels the model silently ignores. Pair with the closed graceful-budget request (#20632) when designing truncation UIs.
  • Agents get better tool plumbing. tool_reference content parts and deferred tools (b11940) plus /v1/realtime tool calls (#31287) mean an OpenAI-shaped tool loop can now span text, audio, and video inputs without a side channel. Validate that your parser handles the new content-part type before rolling forward.
  • Voice/omni agents are viable on CPU-class hardware with LFM3-Audio/Omni-2B and the realtime transcription endpoints — but avoid co-batching multiple sequences of hybrid LFM models until #29002 is resolved; serialize those sessions or use separate contexts.
  • Multi-tenant model routers should adopt --models-memory-max (b11930). It converts hard OOM failures into deterministic evictions, but changes residency semantics — audit any latency SLO that assumed warm models stay loaded.
  • Do not ship speculative decoding with quantized draft/target pairs without output-equality tests against vanilla decoding (#25618). On sm_120 (RTX 50-series) hosts, set GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 until #27330 lands.
  • Cap sampler parameters server-side. Unbounded repeat_last_n/dry_penalty_last_n (#29494) turns a single request into gigabytes of allocation — a one-line validation that every hosted deployment should add today.
  • Pin and verify binaries. Windows CUDA prebuilts lagging at b11828 (#31085) means "latest release" is not a reliable proxy for "latest code" — check the embedded build number, and self-build if you need today's LFM3 or reasoning-effort changes.
Ollama — ollama/ollama

Ollama Digest — 2026-10-28

1. Today's Highlights

No releases landed in the last 24 hours. Activity is concentrated on model enablement and runtime hardening: LFM3 support is being fixed in PR #19344 after users hit issue #19347 and issue #19343, while MLX gains concurrent generation in PR #19197 and CUDA startup crash mitigation in PR #18978. No new releases in the last 24h and no confirmed API/config breaking changes. Compatibility work is in flight but unreleased: stream error forwarding PR #18953, Anthropic thinking-block streaming PR #19110, and OpenAI developer-instruction handling PR #19199 (closed).

  • LFM3 GGUF fixes — PR #19344 (open) fixes BOS handling for LFM3 GGUFs and adds GGUF text-to-speech support; addresses issue #19347 (unknown model architecture: 'lfm3', closed) and issue #19343 (MLX runtime unavailable).

  • MLX concurrent generation — PR #19197 (open) enables multiple simultaneous generation requests via OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL.

  • Feature requests only — GPU acceleration detection in the desktop UI issue #19301; AMD RX 6750 GRE 10GB support issue #19329.

4. Performance & Optimization

  • MLX parallelism — PR #19197 allows MLX models to serve multiple requests concurrently, reducing time-to-first-token for queued requests. Default remains one request; memory must be provisioned per active request.
  • CUDA startup retry — PR #18978 mitigates partial-offload warmup crashes with eager module loading. No throughput numbers provided.
  • Scheduler eviction — issue #19326 reports findRunnerToUnload sorts by sessionDuration then model path; with uniform keep_alive, eviction becomes arbitrary rather than size/recency-based. No fix PR listed.

High severity
